source.text: Παῦλος κλητὸς ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ καὶ Σωσθένης ὁ ἀδελφὸς τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡγιασμένοις ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Κορίνθῳ, κλητοῖς ἁγίοις, σὺν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐπικαλουμένοις τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἡμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Paul, called apostle of Christ Jesus through [the] will of God, and Sosthenes the brother, \v 2 to the church of the God, having been made holy in Christ Jesus, the [one] being in Corinth, called holy [ones], with all the [ones] calling on the name of the Lord of us Jesus Christ in every place, of them and of us;

en.L: Paul, a called apostle of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus through [the] will of God, and Sosthenes [our] brother, \v 2 to the church of God, [to those] made holy in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, [the church] that is in Corinth, called holy ones, together with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} in every place, theirs and ours.
en.B: From Paul, called by the will of God to be an apostle of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, and from Sosthenes our brother, \v 2 to the church of God in Corinth: to you who have been made holy in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, a holy people by God's call, together with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} in every place, the Lord who is theirs as well as ours.
en.R: This letter is from Paul and from our brother Sosthenes. God called me, Paul, to be an apostle, sent out by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. It was God's will. \v 2 We are writing to God's church in the city of Corinth. God has made you holy because you belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. He has called you to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people, together with everyone, everywhere, who prays to our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He is their Lord as well as ours.

fr.L: Paul, appelé [à être] apôtre du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus par la volonté de Dieu, et Sosthène [notre] frère, \v 2 à l’église de Dieu, [à ceux qui ont été] sanctifiés {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, [l’église] qui est à Corinthe, appelés [à être] saints, avec tous ceux qui invoquent le nom de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} en tout lieu, le leur et le nôtre.
fr.B: De la part de Paul, appelé par la volonté de Dieu à être apôtre du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus, et de Sosthène notre frère, \v 2 à l’église de Dieu qui est à Corinthe : à vous qui avez été sanctifiés {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, peuple saint par l’appel de Dieu, avec tous ceux qui, en tout lieu, invoquent le nom de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, leur Seigneur comme le nôtre.
fr.R: Cette lettre vient de Paul et de notre frère Sosthène. Dieu m’a appelé, moi, Paul, à être apôtre, envoyé par le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. C’est Dieu qui l’a voulu. \v 2 Nous écrivons à l’église de Dieu dans la ville de Corinthe. Dieu vous a rendus saints, parce que vous appartenez au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. Il vous a appelés à être {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple saint, avec tous ceux qui, partout, prient notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Il est leur Seigneur comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est le nôtre.

sw.L: Paulo, mtume aliyeitwa wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu kwa mapenzi ya Mungu, na Sosthene ndugu [yetu], \v 2 kwa kanisa la Mungu, kwa waliotakaswa katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, [kanisa] lililoko Korintho, walioitwa [kuwa] watakatifu, pamoja na wote wanaoliitia jina la Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kila mahali, [Bwana] wao na wetu.
sw.B: Kutoka kwa Paulo, aliyeitwa kwa mapenzi ya Mungu kuwa mtume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, na kutoka kwa Sosthene ndugu yetu, \v 2 kwa kanisa la Mungu lililoko Korintho: kwenu ninyi mliotakaswa katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, mlioitwa kuwa watu watakatifu wa Mungu, pamoja na wote wanaoliitia jina la Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kila mahali, aliye Bwana wao na Bwana wetu pia.
sw.R: Barua hii inatoka kwa Paulo na kwa ndugu yetu Sosthene. Mungu aliniita mimi, Paulo, niwe mtume. {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu ndiye aliyenituma, kwa sababu ndivyo Mungu alivyotaka. \v 2 Tunawaandikia ninyi kanisa la Mungu katika mji wa Korintho. Mungu amewafanya kuwa watakatifu kwa sababu ninyi ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Amewaita muwe watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, pamoja na watu wote kila mahali wanaomwomba Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Yeye ni Bwana wao na Bwana wetu pia.

es.L: Pablo, llamado [a ser] apóstol de {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús por [la] voluntad de Dios, y Sóstenes el hermano, \v 2 a la iglesia de Dios, a [los] santificados en {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús, la que está en Corinto, llamados [a ser] santos, junto con todos los que invocan el nombre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} en todo lugar, [Señor] de ellos y nuestro.
es.B: De Pablo, llamado por la voluntad de Dios a ser apóstol {{christos:de Cristo Jesús|del Mesías Jesús}}, y de nuestro hermano Sóstenes, \v 2 a la iglesia de Dios en Corinto: a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} sido santificados en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} y que por el llamado de Dios {{plural_you:son|sois}} un pueblo santo, junto con todos los que en cualquier lugar invocan el nombre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, Señor de ellos y también nuestro.
es.R: Esta carta es de Pablo y de nuestro hermano Sóstenes. Dios me llamó a mí, Pablo, a ser apóstol, enviado por {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}. Así lo quiso Dios. \v 2 Escribimos a la iglesia de Dios en la ciudad de Corinto. Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} ha hecho santos porque {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}. Él {{plural_you:los|os}} ha llamado a ser {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo santo, junto con todos los que, en cualquier lugar, oran a nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Él es Señor de ellos y también nuestro.

vi.L: Phao-lô, sứ đồ được kêu gọi của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} Giê-xu bởi ý muốn của Đức Chúa Trời, và Sốt-then, người anh em [của chúng ta], \v 2 gửi đến Hội Thánh của Đức Chúa Trời, [cho những người] đã được nên thánh trong {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} Giê-xu, [Hội Thánh] ở tại Cô-rinh-tô, là các thánh đồ được kêu gọi, cùng với tất cả những người ở mọi nơi kêu cầu danh Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, của họ cũng như của chúng ta.
vi.B: Phao-lô, người được kêu gọi làm sứ đồ của Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} theo ý muốn của Đức Chúa Trời, cùng với Sốt-then, người anh em của chúng ta, \v 2 kính gửi Hội Thánh của Đức Chúa Trời tại Cô-rinh-tô, là anh chị em, những người đã được nên thánh trong Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} và được Đức Chúa Trời kêu gọi làm dân thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, cùng với tất cả những người ở khắp mọi nơi kêu cầu danh Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, là Chúa của họ cũng như của chúng ta.
vi.R: Thư này của Phao-lô và của Sốt-then, người anh em của chúng ta. Đức Chúa Trời đã gọi tôi, Phao-lô, làm sứ đồ, là người được Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} sai đi. Đó là ý muốn của Đức Chúa Trời. \v 2 Chúng tôi viết thư này cho Hội Thánh của Đức Chúa Trời ở thành Cô-rinh-tô. Đức Chúa Trời đã làm cho anh chị em nên thánh, vì anh chị em thuộc về Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. Ngài đã gọi anh chị em làm dân thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, cùng với mọi người ở khắp nơi đang cầu nguyện với Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. Ngài là Chúa của họ và cũng là Chúa của chúng ta.

ko.L: 하나님의 뜻을 통하여 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수의 사도로 부르심을 받은 바울과 [우리] 형제 소스데네가 \v 2 고린도에 있는 하나님의 교회, 곧 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에서 거룩하게 된 사람들, 부르심을 받은 성도들과, 각처에서 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 이름을 부르는 모든 사람에게 [편지합니다]. [그분은] 그들의 [주님]이시며 우리의 [주님]이십니다.
ko.B: 하나님의 뜻에 따라 부르심을 받아 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수의 사도가 된 바울과 우리 형제 소스데네가 \v 2 고린도에 있는 하나님의 교회에 이 편지를 씁니다. 여러분은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에서 거룩하게 되었고, 하나님의 부르심을 받아 성도가 되었습니다. 어디에서든지 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 이름을 부르는 모든 사람에게도 이 편지를 씁니다. 그분은 그들의 주님이시며 또한 우리의 주님이십니다.
ko.R: 이 편지는 바울과 우리 형제 소스데네가 보냅니다. 하나님께서 나 바울을 부르셔서 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수께서 보내신 사도가 되게 하셨습니다. 그것이 하나님의 뜻이었습니다. \v 2 우리는 고린도라는 도시에 있는 하나님의 교회에 이 편지를 씁니다. 여러분은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수께 속해 있기 때문에 하나님께서 여러분을 거룩하게 하셨습니다. 하나님께서는 여러분을 부르셔서 그분의 거룩한 백성이 되게 하셨습니다. 어디에 있든지 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께 기도하는 모든 사람과 함께 말입니다. 그분은 그들의 주님이시고 우리의 주님이십니다.

pt.L: Paulo, apóstolo chamado {{christos:de Cristo|do Messias}} Jesus pela vontade de Deus, e o irmão Sóstenes, \v 2 à igreja de Deus, [aos] santificados {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus, [a igreja] que está em Corinto, chamados [para serem] santos, juntamente com todos os que invocam o nome do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}} em todo lugar, deles e nosso:
pt.B: De Paulo, chamado pela vontade de Deus para ser apóstolo {{christos:de Cristo|do Messias}} Jesus, e do nosso irmão Sóstenes, \v 2 à igreja de Deus que está em Corinto: a vocês, que foram santificados {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus e chamados por Deus para serem o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo santo, junto com todos os que, em todo lugar, invocam o nome do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, Senhor deles e nosso.
pt.R: Esta carta é de Paulo e do nosso irmão Sóstenes. Eu, Paulo, fui chamado por Deus para ser apóstolo, enviado {{christos:por Cristo|pelo Messias}} Jesus. Essa foi a vontade de Deus. \v 2 Escrevemos à igreja de Deus que está na cidade de Corinto. Deus fez de vocês um povo santo, porque vocês pertencem {{christos:a Cristo|ao Messias}} Jesus. Ele chamou vocês para serem o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo santo, junto com todas as pessoas, em todos os lugares, que oram ao nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}. Ele é o Senhor delas e também o nosso.

decisions.choice: called apostle: an apostle because God called him, a messenger sent out with the authority of the one who sends him
alternatives: an apostle by his own choice
an apostle appointed by a church
decisions.reason: κλητὸς ("called") stands before ἀπόστολος ("apostle"): Paul holds his office because God called him, and "through the will of God" says the same again (compare Galatians 1:1, 1:15). An apostle is one sent out to speak for the one who sends him, as in Colossians 1:1. The same word, κλητοῖς, describes the Corinthians in verse 2: Paul and the church owe their standing to the same call. In a letter to a church that was ranking its teachers (1:12; 9:1-3), Paul rests his authority on God's call, not on his own gifts.

decisions.choice: Sosthenes: a fellow believer known to the Corinthians, perhaps the synagogue leader named in Acts 18:17
decisions.reason: Acts 18:17 tells of a Sosthenes, leader of the synagogue in Corinth, who was beaten in front of the governor Gallio's court. If this is the same man, he had since come to faith and was now with Paul. The name was common, so the link is possible, not certain. "The brother" means a fellow believer.

decisions.choice: the church of God: the assembly of God's people in Corinth, a body of people, not a building, and one that belongs to God
decisions.reason: ἐκκλησίᾳ was the word for the gathered citizen assembly of a Greek city, and the Greek Old Testament uses it for the assembly of Israel gathered before God (Deuteronomy 4:10; 23:1-3). "Of God" says whose it is: not Paul's, Apollos's or Cephas's (1:12), but God's. The first churches met in homes (16:19).

decisions.choice: made holy and called holy: they already belong to God, set apart by him in Christ, and they are holy people because he called them
alternatives: called to become holy, as a goal still to be reached
decisions.reason: ἡγιασμένοις is a perfect participle: they have been made holy, and remain so (6:11). κλητοῖς ἁγίοις means "called holy ones": God's call makes them his holy people, as Israel was (Exodus 19:6; Philippians 1:1). This is what they are, not a prize to be won. It is all the more striking because the letter goes on to correct serious faults in this church. ἡγιασμένοις is masculine plural though "church" is feminine: Paul moves from the church to its people.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "made holy in Christ Jesus" before "that is in Corinth"
alternatives: "to the church of God that is in Corinth, made holy in Christ Jesus"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ in the order of these two phrases. The SBLGNT follows early manuscripts that put "made holy in Christ Jesus" first, which leaves "that is in Corinth" oddly separated from "church"; other manuscripts have the smoother order, which a copyist was more likely to create than to undo. The meaning is the same either way. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: call on the name of the Lord: pray to and worship Jesus as Lord, in the words the Old Testament uses for calling on God
alternatives: simply bear the name of Jesus
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament people "call on the name" of God in prayer and worship (Genesis 4:26; Psalm 116:4), and Joel 2:32 promises that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved; there the Hebrew has God's own name. Paul quotes that verse of Jesus in Romans 10:13. Here the same act of worship is directed to "our Lord Jesus Christ". The Corinthians are reminded that they are one with believers everywhere who do the same.

decisions.choice: theirs and ours: Jesus is their Lord as well as ours
alternatives: in every place, theirs and ours: the places where they and we live
decisions.reason: αὐτῶν καὶ ἡμῶν ("of them and of us") could go with "our Lord" or with "every place". Taken with "Lord", it says that the one Lord belongs to all his people alike, a point the divided Corinthians needed (1:13). Taken with "place", it adds little to "in every place". The Literal keeps the Greek order and leaves the question open.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "called apostle of Christ Jesus"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts reverse the two names, and a few leave out "called". The meaning does not change, so there is no footnote.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: holy ones (L); a holy people (B); God's holy people (R)
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 1:1: in current English "saints" suggests unusually good people or those honored by a church, while Paul is writing to the whole congregation.

decisions.choice: the Lord who is theirs as well as ours (B); He is their Lord as well as ours (R)
alternatives: in every place, theirs and ours
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow meaning decision m7; the Literal keeps the Greek order, which leaves the question open.

decisions.choice: prays to
decisions.reason: "Call on the name" is Bible language for prayer and worship (m6); Readable says it in everyday words.

decisions.choice: This letter is from Paul ... God called me, Paul, to be an apostle ... It was God's will.
alternatives: Paul, called to be an apostle ... through the will of God
decisions.reason: Readable turns the opening of the letter into ordinary sentences, as Philippians 1:1 and Colossians 1:1 do.

decisions.choice: "du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus", "au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}"; "{{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}" for "in Christ"; "Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}" (L), "Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" (B, R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: French cannot say "en Messie", so the span for "in Christ" covers the preposition, with the familiar "en Christ" as the default. Elsewhere the article French needs stays outside the span ("du Christ" / "du Messie"), and is not bracketed at Literal. "Jésus Christ" is written without the hyphen so that both options read naturally.

decisions.choice: l'église de Dieu qui est à Corinthe, lowercase; les saints (L), peuple saint (B, R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The style guide writes "l'église" for one congregation and keeps "l'Église" for the whole body of believers. As in Colossians, "les saints" today suggests exceptionally good people, while Paul writes to the whole congregation, so Balanced and Readable say "peuple saint", as the English does.

decisions.choice: de {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús (L); {{christos:de Cristo Jesús|del Mesías Jesús}}, {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}} (B, R); {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}} (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans, Galatians and Colossians: Spanish puts the article before "Mesías" but not before "Cristo", and "de el" and "a el" contract to "del" and "al", so at Balanced and Readable the span takes in the preposition. Literal follows the Greek, which has no article here, as the English Literal does. For "Jesus Christ" the default is the usual Spanish name "Jesucristo", and the alternative separates name and title. The same holds for the rest of the letter.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Paul writes to the Corinthian church in the plural throughout. Every plural "you" addressed to the readers, with its pronouns and verbs, is a reader setting: ustedes forms (Latin America, the default) or vosotros forms (Spain), as "{{plural_you:han|habéis}} sido santificados" here. Each span covers only the words that differ.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives (wake, yake, yeye, naye)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun, as in English
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God and Christ inside the verb ("aliniita", "amewaita"), and a prefix cannot take a capital. So in these chapters the deity_pronoun setting applies only to the free pronouns and possessives, and Swahili has fewer spans than the English.

decisions.choice: waliotakaswa ... watakatifu (L); mliotakaswa ... watu watakatifu wa Mungu (B); amewafanya kuwa watakatifu ... watu wake (R)
decisions.reason: "Kutakaswa" (to be made holy) and "watakatifu" (holy ones) share one root in Swahili as the two Greek words do, so the link the meaning decision draws between being made holy and being called holy stays visible. The holy ones are "watakatifu" (L), "watu watakatifu wa Mungu" (B) and "watu wa Mungu" (R) through the letter, as in the other Swahili letters.

decisions.choice: "tôi" for Paul, "chúng tôi" for Paul with Sosthenes or his fellow workers, "chúng ta" where the readers are included, and "anh chị em" for "you" (plural) through the whole letter
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Romans, Galatians and Colossians: Vietnamese has no neutral "you", and "anh chị em" is the warm, inclusive word Vietnamese churches use. It is plain text here, not a gender span, since the Greek pronoun has no word for brothers; the span is kept for adelphoi. Paul calls them his children only where he says so himself (4:14-15), and the Vietnamese follows him there.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} Giê-xu (L), Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} (B, R) for "Christ Jesus"; Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} for "our Lord Jesus Christ"; {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} for "Christ" alone
decisions.reason: The forms of the Vietnamese Romans and Colossians, kept through both letters to Corinth: Literal keeps the Greek order, title first; Balanced and Readable use the name with the title after it.

decisions.choice: "Hội Thánh" for the church; "các thánh đồ" (L), "dân thánh của Đức Chúa Trời" (B, R) for the holy ones; "được nên thánh" for "made holy" (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Hội Thánh" is the church word of the Vietnamese Romans and Galatians. "Thánh đồ" keeps the one Greek word at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "God's holy people", so that the whole church is plainly meant (m4), as in Colossians. "Được nên thánh" is the verb of "sự nên thánh" in Romans 6:19.

decisions.choice: "Sốt-then", "Cô-rinh-tô", and the other names of the letter in the Protestant transliterations (Cơ-lô-ê, A-bô-lô, Sê-pha, Cơ-rít-bu, Gai-út, Sê-pha-na)
decisions.reason: The style guide follows the Protestant tradition's forms of names, which most Vietnamese Bible readers know; "Cô-rinh-tô" is the form already used in 2 Timothy 4:20.

decisions.choice: the whole letter in 합쇼체 (-습니다, -십시오) at every level; the readers are "여러분"; Paul speaks of himself as "나" and "우리"; God, Christ and the Holy Spirit take the subject honorific (-시-, 께서); no deity_pronoun spans
alternatives: 해라체 (-다, -라), the style of the older Korean Bibles
the humble "저" and "저희" for Paul and his companions
decisions.reason: As in Romans, Galatians and the other letters already drafted, a letter to a whole church, read aloud when it gathered, calls for the formal style of a letter and a public address, so every level uses 합쇼체 and its imperatives (-십시오), with "여러분" for the plural "you". Paul writes as an apostle with authority over the church he founded (4:14-21), so he says "나" and "우리" rather than the humble forms. Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change and the Korean text has no deity_pronoun spans: respect for God and Christ is carried by "그분" and the honorific on verbs and subjects. Quoted slogans and Scripture keep their own style.

decisions.choice: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} at every level, "예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}" with the name; {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들 for the believers, through the letter
alternatives: the Messiah, with an article Korean does not have
decisions.reason: Korean has no article, so the christos alternative is plain "메시아" at every level, and both words end in a vowel, so one particle fits either. "형제자매" (brothers and sisters) is the inclusive default for believers, with "형제" as the traditional form; a man named alone, as Sosthenes here, is plainly "형제".

decisions.choice: "사도", "교회" at every level; "성도" (L, B) and "하나님의 거룩한 백성" (R) for the holy ones; "부르심을 받다" for being called, through the letter
decisions.reason: These are the words of Romans and the other letters. "성도" is the ordinary Korean church word for every believer, and does not suggest unusually good people; Readable says what it means, "하나님의 거룩한 백성". "부르심" is God's call, and the same word joins Paul's call (verse 1) and the church's (verses 2, 9, 24, 26).

decisions.choice: "[그분은] 그들의 [주님]이시며 우리의 [주님]이십니다" (L), a sentence of its own
decisions.reason: Korean cannot attach "theirs and ours" to "Lord" at the end of the sentence, so Literal and Balanced say it as a short sentence after it, with the reading of the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: a igreja de Deus que está em Corinto
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as docs/portuguese-style.md section 6 sets it: "igreja" in lowercase for one congregation ("a igreja de Deus que está em Corinto", "as igrejas"), with a capital only where the word means the whole body of believers. "Assembleia" would be closer to the Greek word's everyday sense, but m3 already explains it, and Brazilian readers know the congregation as "a igreja".

decisions.choice: chamados [para serem] santos (L); chamados por Deus para serem o seu povo santo (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Romans and as the style guide sets it. In Brazil "os santos" suggests a few canonised people; m4 says Paul means the whole congregation, set apart by God's call, so Balanced and Readable say "povo santo". Literal keeps "santos". "Santificados" (L, B) stands for the perfect participle "made holy".

decisions.choice: apóstolo {{christos:de Cristo|do Messias}} Jesus; {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus
decisions.reason: For the whole book. Portuguese contracts the preposition with the article of "o Messias" ("do", "no", "ao", "pelo"), so the preposition goes inside both options of the title setting; otherwise the alternative would read "de o Messias".

source.text: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Grace to you and peace from God Father of us and Lord Jesus Christ.

en.L: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: I pray that God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will show you grace and give you peace.

fr.L: Grâce à vous et paix de la part de Dieu notre Père et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Grâce et paix à vous de la part de Dieu notre Père et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Je prie pour que Dieu notre Père et le Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} vous accordent la grâce et la paix.

sw.L: Neema kwenu na amani kutoka kwa Mungu Baba yetu na Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Neema na amani ziwe nanyi kutoka kwa Mungu Baba yetu na kutoka kwa Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Ninaomba kwamba Mungu Baba yetu na Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} wawaonyeshe neema na kuwapa amani.

es.L: Gracia a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y paz de Dios nuestro Padre y [del] Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Gracia y paz a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} de parte de Dios nuestro Padre y del Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Pido que Dios nuestro Padre y el Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} {{plural_you:les|os}} muestren {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia y {{plural_you:les|os}} den paz.

vi.L: Ân điển cho anh chị em và bình an từ Đức Chúa Trời, Cha chúng ta, và Chúa Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Nguyện ân điển và bình an từ Đức Chúa Trời, Cha chúng ta, và từ Chúa Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} ở cùng anh chị em.
vi.R: Cầu xin Đức Chúa Trời, Cha chúng ta, và Chúa Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} ban ân điển và bình an cho anh chị em.

ko.L: 하나님 우리 아버지와 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께로부터 은혜와 평안이 여러분에게 [있기를 빕니다].
ko.B: 하나님 우리 아버지와 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 여러분에게 은혜와 평안을 주시기를 빕니다.
ko.R: 우리 아버지 하나님과 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 여러분에게 은혜를 베푸시고 평안을 주시기를 기도합니다.

pt.L: Graça a vocês e paz da parte de Deus, nosso Pai, e [do] Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}.
pt.B: Graça e paz a vocês da parte de Deus, nosso Pai, e do Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.
pt.R: Oro para que Deus, nosso Pai, e o Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} deem graça e paz a vocês.

decisions.choice: one source: God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ together
decisions.reason: A single ἀπὸ ("from") governs both names, so Jesus is named with God the Father as the one source of grace and peace. Paul opens almost every letter this way (Romans 1:7; Philippians 1:2).

decisions.choice: a greeting turned into a blessing
decisions.reason: Greek letters normally opened with a one-word "greetings". Paul replaces it with χάρις (grace), a word close to it in sound, and adds εἰρήνη (peace), the usual Jewish greeting. It is a wish and a prayer for God's favor and wholeness.

decisions.choice: Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: I pray that ... will show you grace and give you peace
decisions.reason: The greeting has no verb. Readable states it as the prayer it is, as Philippians 1:2 does.

decisions.choice: "은혜와 평안" at every level, through the letter
decisions.reason: The words of the greeting in Romans and the other letters: "은혜" is a key term, and "평안" is the peace God gives, as in John 14:27. "평화" is kept for peace between people (7:15; 14:33).

source.text: Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῇ χάριτι τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ δοθείσῃ ὑμῖν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ὅτι ἐν παντὶ ἐπλουτίσθητε ἐν αὐτῷ, ἐν παντὶ λόγῳ καὶ πάσῃ γνώσει, καθὼς τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐβεβαιώθη ἐν ὑμῖν, ὥστε ὑμᾶς μὴ ὑστερεῖσθαι ἐν μηδενὶ χαρίσματι, ἀπεκδεχομένους τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: I give thanks to the God of me always concerning you for the grace of the God the [one] having been given to you in Christ Jesus, \v 5 that in everything you were made rich in him, in all speech and all knowledge, \v 6 just as the testimony of the Christ was confirmed in you, \v 7 so that you not to be lacking in no gift, awaiting the revelation of the Lord of us Jesus Christ;

en.L: I thank my God always concerning you for the grace of God that was given to you in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, \v 5 that in everything you were made rich in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, in all speech and all knowledge, \v 6 just as the testimony of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} was confirmed in you, \v 7 so that you do not lack any gift, as you wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: I give thanks to my God for you at all times, because of the grace God gave you in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. \v 5 In {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you have been made rich in everything: in every kind of speaking and every kind of knowledge. \v 6 In this way the witness to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} was made firm among you, \v 7 and so you fall short in no gift of grace while you wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: I always thank my God for you, because of the grace {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given you in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. \v 5 Because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, God has made you rich in every way: in all you say and in all you know. \v 6 This shows that the message we told you about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has taken firm root in you. \v 7 So you have every gift that God in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace gives, while you wait for the day when our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will appear.

fr.L: Je rends grâce à mon Dieu toujours à votre sujet pour la grâce de Dieu qui vous a été donnée {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, \v 5 parce qu’en tout vous avez été enrichis en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, en toute parole et toute connaissance, \v 6 selon que le témoignage du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} a été affermi en vous, \v 7 de sorte que vous ne manquez d’aucun don, attendant la révélation de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Je rends grâce à mon Dieu pour vous en tout temps, à cause de la grâce que Dieu vous a donnée {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus. \v 5 En {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, vous avez été enrichis en toutes choses : en toute sorte de parole et en toute sorte de connaissance. \v 6 C’est ainsi que le témoignage rendu au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} s’est affermi parmi vous, \v 7 si bien qu’aucun don de la grâce ne vous fait défaut, tandis que vous attendez la révélation de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Je remercie toujours mon Dieu pour vous, à cause de la grâce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous a donnée {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus. \v 5 Parce que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartenez, Dieu vous a rendus riches de toutes les manières : dans tout ce que vous dites et dans tout ce que vous savez. \v 6 Cela montre que le message que nous vous avons annoncé au sujet du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} a pris solidement racine en vous. \v 7 Ainsi, vous avez tous les dons que Dieu donne dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce, pendant que vous attendez le jour où notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} apparaîtra.

sw.L: Ninamshukuru Mungu wangu siku zote kuhusu ninyi kwa ajili ya neema ya Mungu mliyopewa katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, \v 5 kwamba katika kila jambo mlitajirishwa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, katika kila usemi na katika maarifa yote, \v 6 kama vile ushuhuda wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ulivyothibitishwa ndani yenu, \v 7 hata hampungukiwi na karama yoyote, mkingoja kufunuliwa kwa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Ninamshukuru Mungu wangu kwa ajili yenu wakati wote, kwa sababu ya neema ambayo Mungu aliwapa katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. \v 5 Ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mmetajirishwa katika kila jambo: katika kila namna ya kusema na kila namna ya maarifa. \v 6 Kwa njia hiyo ushuhuda kuhusu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ulithibitishwa imara kati yenu, \v 7 na hivyo hampungukiwi na karama yoyote ya neema mnapongoja kufunuliwa kwa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Siku zote ninamshukuru Mungu wangu kwa ajili yenu, kwa sababu ya neema aliyowapa katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. \v 5 Kwa kuwa ninyi ni {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, Mungu amewatajirisha kwa kila namna: katika yote mnayosema na katika yote mnayojua. \v 6 Hii inaonyesha kwamba ujumbe tuliowaambia kuhusu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} umeota mizizi imara ndani yenu. \v 7 Kwa hiyo mna kila karama ambayo Mungu hutoa kwa neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, mnapongoja siku ambapo Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} atatokea.

es.L: Doy gracias a mi Dios siempre por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} por la gracia de Dios que {{plural_you:les|os}} fue dada en {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús, \v 5 porque en todo {{plural_you:fueron enriquecidos|fuisteis enriquecidos}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, en toda palabra y en todo conocimiento, \v 6 así como el testimonio del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} fue confirmado en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \v 7 de modo que no {{plural_you:les|os}} falta ningún don, mientras {{plural_you:esperan|esperáis}} la revelación de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Doy gracias a mi Dios por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en todo momento, a causa de la gracia que Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} dio en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}. \v 5 En {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:han|habéis}} sido enriquecidos en todo: en toda clase de palabra y en toda clase de conocimiento. \v 6 Así el testimonio acerca {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} se afirmó entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \v 7 y por eso no {{plural_you:les|os}} falta ningún don de la gracia mientras {{plural_you:esperan|esperáis}} la revelación de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Siempre doy gracias a mi Dios por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, por la gracia que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}. \v 5 Porque {{plural_you:pertenecen|pertenecéis}} a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} ha hecho ricos en todo: en todo lo que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} y en todo lo que {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}}. \v 6 Esto muestra que el mensaje que {{plural_you:les|os}} anunciamos acerca {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} ha echado raíces firmes en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \v 7 Por eso {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} todos los dones que Dios da por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, mientras {{plural_you:esperan|esperáis}} el día en que nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} aparezca.

vi.L: Tôi luôn luôn tạ ơn Đức Chúa Trời của tôi về anh chị em, vì ân điển của Đức Chúa Trời đã được ban cho anh chị em trong {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} Giê-xu, \v 5 rằng trong mọi sự anh chị em đã được làm cho giàu có trong {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, trong mọi lời nói và mọi tri thức, \v 6 cũng như lời chứng của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã được làm cho vững chắc trong anh chị em, \v 7 đến nỗi anh chị em không thiếu một ân tứ nào, trong khi trông đợi sự hiện ra của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Tôi luôn tạ ơn Đức Chúa Trời của tôi về anh chị em, vì ân điển Đức Chúa Trời đã ban cho anh chị em trong Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. \v 5 Trong {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, anh chị em đã được làm cho giàu có về mọi mặt: trong mọi cách nói và mọi tri thức. \v 6 Như vậy, lời chứng về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã được củng cố vững vàng giữa anh chị em, \v 7 nên anh chị em không thiếu một ân tứ nào trong khi trông đợi Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} hiện ra.
vi.R: Tôi luôn cảm tạ Đức Chúa Trời của tôi về anh chị em, vì ân điển {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban cho anh chị em trong Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. \v 5 Vì anh chị em thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, Đức Chúa Trời đã làm cho anh chị em giàu có về mọi mặt: trong mọi điều anh chị em nói và mọi điều anh chị em biết. \v 6 Điều đó cho thấy sứ điệp chúng tôi đã rao truyền cho anh chị em về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã đâm rễ vững chắc trong anh chị em. \v 7 Vì vậy, anh chị em có đủ mọi món quà mà Đức Chúa Trời ban cho bởi ân điển của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, trong khi chờ đợi ngày Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} hiện đến.

ko.L: 나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에서 여러분에게 주어진 하나님의 은혜 때문에 여러분에 대하여 언제나 나의 하나님께 감사합니다. \v 5 여러분이 모든 일에 그분 안에서 부요하게 되었으니, 곧 모든 말과 모든 지식에서 [그렇게 되었습니다]. \v 6 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}에 대한 증언이 여러분 가운데서 확실해진 것과 같이, \v 7 여러분은 어떤 은사에도 부족함이 없이 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 나타나시기를 기다리고 있습니다.
ko.B: 나는 하나님께서 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에서 여러분에게 주신 은혜를 생각하며, 여러분 때문에 언제나 나의 하나님께 감사드립니다. \v 5 여러분은 그분 안에서 모든 일에 부요하게 되었습니다. 온갖 말과 온갖 지식이 풍성해졌습니다. \v 6 이렇게 해서 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}에 대한 증언이 여러분 가운데서 굳게 섰습니다. \v 7 그래서 여러분은 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 나타나실 날을 기다리면서, 은혜의 선물인 은사를 하나도 빠짐없이 받았습니다.
ko.R: 나는 여러분 때문에 언제나 나의 하나님께 감사드립니다. 하나님께서 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에서 여러분에게 은혜를 주셨기 때문입니다. \v 5 여러분이 그분께 속해 있기 때문에 하나님께서는 여러분을 모든 면에서 부요하게 하셨습니다. 여러분이 하는 모든 말과 여러분이 아는 모든 것이 풍성해졌습니다. \v 6 이것을 보면, 우리가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}에 대해 전한 소식이 여러분 안에 깊이 뿌리내렸다는 것을 알 수 있습니다. \v 7 그래서 여러분에게는 하나님께서 은혜로 주시는 은사가 다 있습니다. 여러분은 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 나타나실 날을 기다리고 있습니다.

pt.L: Dou graças ao meu Deus sempre a respeito de vocês, pela graça de Deus que foi dada a vocês {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus, \v 5 porque em tudo vocês foram enriquecidos {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}, em toda palavra e em todo conhecimento, \v 6 assim como o testemunho do {{christos:Cristo|Messias}} foi confirmado em vocês, \v 7 de modo que não lhes falta nenhum dom, enquanto aguardam a revelação do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}.
pt.B: Agradeço ao meu Deus por vocês em todo tempo, por causa da graça que Deus lhes deu {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus. \v 5 Nele vocês foram enriquecidos em tudo: em todo tipo de palavra e em todo tipo de conhecimento. \v 6 Assim o testemunho sobre {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} se firmou entre vocês, \v 7 e por isso não lhes falta nenhum dom da graça, enquanto vocês aguardam a revelação do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.
pt.R: Sempre agradeço ao meu Deus por vocês, por causa da graça que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} deu a vocês {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus. \v 5 Porque vocês pertencem a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, Deus os tornou ricos em tudo: em tudo o que vocês falam e em tudo o que vocês sabem. \v 6 Isso mostra que a mensagem que anunciamos a vocês sobre {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} criou raízes firmes em vocês. \v 7 Por isso vocês têm todos os dons que Deus, na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} graça, dá, enquanto esperam o dia em que o nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} vai aparecer.

decisions.choice: the grace given in Christ Jesus: God's free favor, given when they came to belong to Christ and seen in their gifts (verses 5-7)
decisions.reason: δοθείσῃ ("given") is an aorist and points back to a definite time, when the Corinthians believed. "In Christ Jesus" says where the gift is found: in union with him. Verses 5-7 then say what the grace has produced among them.

decisions.choice: speech and knowledge: gifts of speaking (teaching, prophecy, tongues) and of understanding God's ways
alternatives: eloquence and learning as human skills
decisions.reason: λόγῳ and γνώσει name things the Corinthians prized, and the letter comes back to both (8:1; 12:8; 13:1-2; 14:1-25). Paul thanks God for them as gifts before he corrects the way the church uses them.

decisions.choice: the testimony about Christ, made firm among them
alternatives: the testimony that Christ himself gave
decisions.reason: Χριστοῦ names whom the testimony is about: the message Paul bore witness to when he came to Corinth (2:1-2; 15:15). ἐβεβαιώθη means confirmed or made firm, a word also used for a legal guarantee (compare Philippians 1:7). The gifts the church received showed that the message had taken hold.

decisions.choice: gift: a particular gift of God's grace
alternatives: only the miraculous gifts of the Spirit
decisions.reason: χαρίσματι is built from the word for grace and means something given freely. Paul uses it for any gift of grace (Romans 6:23; 1 Corinthians 7:7), including the gifts of the Spirit discussed in chapters 12-14. The link with the grace of verse 4 is deliberate.

decisions.choice: the revealing of the Lord: his coming in glory at the end, for which they eagerly wait
decisions.reason: ἀποκάλυψιν is an unveiling. Paul uses it of the Lord Jesus being revealed from heaven (2 Thessalonians 1:7), and verse 8 speaks of "the day of our Lord". ἀπεκδεχομένους is a strong word for eager waiting (Philippians 3:20). The gifts belong to this time of waiting, not to the end itself (13:8-12).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "my God"
decisions.reason: A few important early manuscripts do not have "my". It is easy to see a copyist either adding it from Philippians 1:3 or dropping it. The meaning is not changed.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article in verse 6: "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}".

decisions.choice: gift of grace (B); every gift that God in his grace gives (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the link with "grace" in verse 4 that the Greek word carries (m4).

decisions.choice: Because you belong to him; This shows that the message we told you about Christ has taken firm root in you; the day when our Lord Jesus Christ will appear
alternatives: just as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you
the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in him" means, how the gifts show that the message took hold (m3), and what the "revealing" of the Lord is (m5).

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level (for the whole letter)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: 1 Corinthians is a letter: Paul speaks to the readers about what God has done among them ("vous avez été enrichis", "le témoignage ... a été affermi"), and French uses the passé composé for that, as in Colossians.

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" included (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for God or Christ carries the span, and so do pronouns French needs where English has none ("vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartenez" in verse 5). A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital. The Holy Spirit takes the same setting.

decisions.choice: palabra
decisions.reason: The Greek word here means speech, every kind of speaking (m2). Literal keeps "palabra", which in Spanish also names the gift of speaking; Balanced says "toda clase de palabra" so it is not read as one single word.

decisions.choice: karama
decisions.reason: "Karama" is the Swahili word for a gift given by God's grace (Romans 1:11; 11:29), and it is kept for this Greek word through the letter, so the gifts of chapters 12–14 can be traced back to here. "Zawadi" is any present.

decisions.choice: "ân tứ" (L, B); "món quà mà Đức Chúa Trời ban cho bởi ân điển" (R) for charisma here
decisions.reason: "Ân tứ" is the word of the Vietnamese Romans (1:11; 12:6) for a gift of God's grace, and it keeps the link with "ân điển" (grace) that the Greek has. Readable says what the gift is, as Romans does. In chapters 12-14, where the gifts are the subject, Readable keeps "ân tứ" too, so the word can be followed.

decisions.choice: "tri thức" for gnosis; "sự hiện ra" (L), "hiện ra" (B), "hiện đến" (R) for the revealing of the Lord
decisions.reason: "Tri thức" is kept for gnosis, as in Colossians 2:3, so that "knowledge" can be followed into chapter 8 and 13. For the Lord's coming, "hiện ra" is the word of 2 Thessalonians 1:7; "sự mặc khải" would suggest a message revealed rather than a person appearing.

decisions.choice: "은사" at every level for the gift of grace, with "은혜의 선물인" (B) and "하나님께서 은혜로 주시는" (R), here and through chapters 12-14
decisions.reason: "은사" is the word of Romans 12:6 and 1 Timothy 4:14 for a gift God gives in his grace; it shares its first syllable with "은혜" (grace), as the Greek word shares its root with grace. "영적인 은사" is kept for the different word of 12:1 and 14:1.

decisions.choice: Readable gives the reason for thanks as its own sentence after "감사드립니다"
alternatives: one long sentence as in Literal
decisions.reason: Short sentences, as the level asks; the content of each verse stays after its marker.

decisions.choice: dom (L); dom da graça (B); os dons que Deus, na sua graça, dá (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as docs/corinthians-terms.md sets "gift": "dom", never "dom espiritual", which is kept for the different word of 12:1. Balanced and Readable keep the link with "graça" in verse 4 (m4), as the English does.

source.text: ὃς καὶ βεβαιώσει ὑμᾶς ἕως τέλους ἀνεγκλήτους ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: who also will confirm you until [the] end blameless in the day of the Lord of us Jesus Christ.

en.L: [He] who will also confirm you to [the] end, blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: He will also keep you firm to the end, so that you will be free from any charge on the day of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: He will keep you strong to the very end, so that no one will be able to accuse you of anything on the day our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} comes back.

fr.L: [C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}] qui vous affermira aussi jusqu’à la fin, irréprochables au jour de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Il vous gardera aussi fermes jusqu’à la fin, pour que vous soyez à l’abri de toute accusation au jour de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Il vous gardera forts jusqu’au bout. Ainsi, personne ne pourra vous accuser de rien le jour où notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} reviendra.

sw.L: [Yeye] ambaye pia atawathibitisha hadi mwisho, [mkiwa] bila lawama katika siku ya Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Yeye pia atawaimarisha hadi mwisho, ili msiwe na lawama yoyote katika siku ya Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Atawaimarisha mpaka mwisho kabisa, ili siku ile Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} atakaporudi, mtu yeyote asiweze kuwashtaki kwa jambo lolote.

es.L: [Él] también {{plural_you:los|os}} confirmará hasta [el] fin, irreprochables en el día de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Él también {{plural_you:los|os}} mantendrá firmes hasta el fin, para que {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} libres de toda acusación en el día de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Él {{plural_you:los|os}} mantendrá fuertes hasta el final, para que nadie pueda {{plural_you:acusarlos|acusaros}} de nada el día en que nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} regrese.

vi.L: [Ngài là] Đấng cũng sẽ làm cho anh chị em vững vàng cho đến cuối cùng, không chỗ trách được trong ngày của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Ngài cũng sẽ giữ anh chị em vững vàng đến cuối cùng, để anh chị em không bị ai buộc tội điều gì trong ngày của Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.R: Ngài sẽ giữ cho anh chị em mạnh mẽ đến tận cuối cùng, để không ai có thể tố cáo anh chị em điều gì vào ngày Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} trở lại.

ko.L: 그분은 여러분을 끝까지 굳게 세우셔서, 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 날에 책망받을 것이 없는 [사람이 되게] 하실 것입니다.
ko.B: 그분은 또한 여러분을 끝까지 굳게 지켜 주셔서, 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 날에 아무 흠도 잡히지 않게 하실 것입니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 여러분을 끝까지 강하게 지켜 주실 것입니다. 그래서 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 다시 오시는 날에 아무도 여러분을 고발할 수 없을 것입니다.

pt.L: O qual também os confirmará até [o] fim, irrepreensíveis no dia do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}.
pt.B: Ele também os manterá firmes até o fim, para que vocês estejam livres de qualquer acusação no dia do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}.
pt.R: Ele vai manter vocês firmes até o fim, para que ninguém possa acusar vocês de nada no dia em que o nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} voltar.

decisions.choice: who: most likely God, who gave the grace (verse 4) and whose faithfulness verse 9 names; the words may also point to Jesus Christ, named just before
decisions.reason: The relative pronoun ὃς most naturally refers to the last person named, Jesus Christ at the end of verse 7. But the sentence goes on to "the day of our Lord Jesus Christ", which reads oddly if Christ is the subject, and verse 9 gives the ground of this promise: "God is faithful." Every level keeps the subject unnamed ("who", "He"), as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: confirm, keep firm: God will hold them steady and secure
decisions.reason: βεβαιώσει is the verb of verse 6 again: as the message about Christ was made firm among them, so they themselves will be made firm. The word was also used of a legal guarantee.

decisions.choice: blameless: with no charge that can be brought against them
decisions.reason: ἀνεγκλήτους is a word from the law court: no accusation will stand (compare Colossians 1:22). Paul pictures the coming day as a judgment at which they will be found clear.

decisions.choice: the day of our Lord: the Old Testament day of God's judgment, now the day of Jesus' coming
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of "the day of the Lord", when God would come to judge and to save (Amos 5:18; Joel 2:31). Paul gives the day to Jesus (5:5; Philippians 1:6), connecting it with his "revealing" in verse 7.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "our Lord Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts end the verse with "Jesus" and do not have "Christ". The meaning does not change. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: [He] who (L); He (B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level leaves the subject unnamed, so as not to decide what the Greek leaves open (m1). A sentence beginning with a bare "who" is not possible in English, so Literal supplies "[He]".

decisions.choice: free from any charge (B); no one will be able to accuse you of anything (R)
decisions.reason: "Blameless" can sound like a claim of perfect behavior. Balanced and Readable keep the law-court sense (m3), as Colossians 1:22 does.

decisions.choice: [C'est lui] qui
decisions.reason: French cannot begin a sentence with a bare relative "qui". The supplied words, like the English "[He]", leave open whether God or Christ is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: [Él] (L); Él (B, R), no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The verse begins a new sentence with the relative "who", which most likely means God (m1). Spanish "Él" at the start of a sentence is capitalised either way, so it takes no deity_pronoun span, as the English "He" does not; it also keeps open, like the Greek, whether God or Christ is meant.

decisions.choice: "ngày của Chúa" (L, B); "ngày Chúa ... trở lại" (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Thessalonians 5:2: Readable says plainly which day is meant.

decisions.choice: "하나님께서는" (R) for "who"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "who" as God, most likely; Literal and Balanced keep "그분" as the Greek's pronoun, and Readable names God, as the English Readable keeps "He" after God in verse 4.

decisions.choice: O qual
decisions.reason: Portuguese can open a sentence with the relative "O qual", which keeps the Greek's link to what comes before without naming God or Christ (m1); English needs a supplied "[He]".

source.text: πιστὸς ὁ θεὸς δι’ οὗ ἐκλήθητε εἰς κοινωνίαν τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Faithful [is] the God, through whom you were called into fellowship of the Son of him, Jesus Christ the Lord of us.

en.L: God [is] faithful, through whom you were called into [the] fellowship of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} our Lord.
en.B: God is faithful. It was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who called you to share in the life of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} our Lord.
en.R: You can depend on God. He is the one who called you to be joined to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} our Lord, and to share {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life.

fr.L: Dieu [est] fidèle, par qui vous avez été appelés à la communion de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}} notre Seigneur.
fr.B: Dieu est fidèle. C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui vous a appelés à partager la vie de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} notre Seigneur.
fr.R: Vous pouvez compter sur Dieu. C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui vous a appelés à être unis à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} notre Seigneur, et à partager {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} vie.

sw.L: Mungu [ni] mwaminifu, ambaye kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} mliitwa katika ushirika wa Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Bwana wetu.
sw.B: Mungu ni mwaminifu. Yeye ndiye aliyewaita muwe na ushirika na Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Bwana wetu.
sw.R: Mnaweza kumtegemea Mungu. Yeye ndiye aliyewaita mwunganishwe na Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Bwana wetu, na mshiriki uzima {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

es.L: Fiel [es] Dios, por medio de quien {{plural_you:fueron llamados|fuisteis llamados}} a [la] comunión de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, nuestro Señor.
es.B: Dios es fiel. Fue {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quien {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó a participar en la vida de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, nuestro Señor.
es.R: {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} confiar en Dios. Él es quien {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó a estar unidos a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, nuestro Señor, y a compartir {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} vida.

vi.L: Đức Chúa Trời [là Đấng] thành tín, bởi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} anh chị em đã được kêu gọi vào sự thông công với Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, Chúa chúng ta.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời là Đấng thành tín. Chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã kêu gọi anh chị em để dự phần trong sự sống của Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, Chúa chúng ta.
vi.R: Anh chị em có thể tin cậy Đức Chúa Trời. Chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã gọi anh chị em để được gắn bó với Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, Chúa chúng ta, và cùng chia sẻ sự sống của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 하나님은 신실하십니다. 그분을 통하여 여러분은 그분의 아들 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}와의 사귐으로 부르심을 받았습니다.
ko.B: 하나님은 신실하신 분입니다. 그분이 여러분을 부르셔서 그분의 아들, 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}와 함께 생명을 나누게 하셨습니다.
ko.R: 하나님은 믿을 수 있는 분입니다. 그분이 여러분을 부르셔서 그분의 아들, 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}와 하나가 되게 하시고 그분의 생명을 함께 누리게 하셨습니다.

pt.L: Fiel [é] Deus, por meio de quem vocês foram chamados para [a] comunhão do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho, Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}, nosso Senhor.
pt.B: Deus é fiel. Foi {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quem chamou vocês para participarem da vida do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho, Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, nosso Senhor.
pt.R: Vocês podem contar com Deus. Foi {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} quem chamou vocês para ficarem unidos ao {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho, Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, nosso Senhor, e participarem da vida {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

decisions.choice: faithful: God can be relied on to keep his word and finish what he began
decisions.reason: πιστὸς here means trustworthy. The promise of verse 8 rests on God's faithfulness, as it does in 10:13 and 1 Thessalonians 5:24. It stands first in the sentence for emphasis.

decisions.choice: through whom you were called: God himself is the one who called them
alternatives: God called them through someone else
decisions.reason: "Through" usually names a go-between, but here οὗ ("whom") is God himself, as in Romans 11:36. The call is God's own act, the call that made them "called holy ones" (verse 2).

decisions.choice: fellowship of his Son: a shared life with the Son, and in him with one another
alternatives: partnership in a task (as in Philippians 1:5)
decisions.reason: κοινωνίαν means having a share in something together. With "of his Son" it means sharing in the Son himself: belonging to him and having a part in his life (compare 10:16, where the cup is a sharing in the blood of Christ). The word prepares for the appeal of verse 10: people who all share in one Son cannot be divided into parties.

decisions.choice: his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord: the opening names Jesus as Lord again and again
decisions.reason: In verses 1-10 Paul names "our Lord Jesus Christ" in nearly every sentence. Here the full title closes the thanksgiving: the one the Corinthians share is God's own Son and their Lord, not any human teacher.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: share in the life of (B); be joined to ... and to share his life (R)
decisions.reason: "Fellowship" today often means a friendly gathering. Balanced and Readable say what it means here (m3).

decisions.choice: You can depend on God
decisions.reason: Readable says what "faithful" means here (m1).

decisions.choice: ushirika
decisions.reason: "Ushirika" is sharing in a common life, which is the sense the meaning decision gives; Readable spells it out as being joined to the Son and sharing his life ("uzima").

decisions.choice: "sự thông công với" (L); "dự phần trong sự sống của" (B); "được gắn bó với ... và cùng chia sẻ sự sống" (R) for koinonia
decisions.reason: "Sự thông công" is the church word for koinonia, kept at Literal as in Philippians 2:1; to many readers it now means a church meeting, so Balanced and Readable say what it is, a shared life with the Son (m3).

decisions.choice: "사귐" (L); "함께 생명을 나누다" (B); "하나가 되다 ... 함께 누리다" (R)
decisions.reason: "교제" now sounds like social contact or dating; "사귐" keeps the older sense of a shared life, and Balanced and Readable say what is shared, as the English does.

source.text: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἵνα τὸ αὐτὸ λέγητε πάντες, καὶ μὴ ᾖ ἐν ὑμῖν σχίσματα, ἦτε δὲ κατηρτισμένοι ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ νοῒ καὶ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ γνώμῃ.

records.literal_gloss: I urge but you, brothers, through the name of the Lord of us Jesus Christ, that the same [thing] you say all, and not be among you divisions, you be but having been restored in the same mind and in the same judgment.

en.L: Now I urge you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, by the name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, that you all say the same thing, and [that] there be no divisions among you, but [that] you be restored in the same mind and in the same judgment.
en.B: Now, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I urge you by the name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}: agree with one another, all of you, and let there be no splits among you. Let what is torn be mended, so that you are joined together, one in mind and one in purpose.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I urge you in the name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}: agree with each other. Do not split up into groups. Be united again, so that you share the same way of thinking and the same goals.

fr.L: Or je vous exhorte, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, par le nom de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, à dire tous la même chose, et qu’il n’y ait pas de divisions parmi vous, mais que vous soyez rétablis dans la même pensée et dans le même avis.
fr.B: Or, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, je vous en prie instamment par le nom de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} : mettez-vous d’accord, vous tous, et qu’il n’y ait pas de déchirures parmi vous. Que ce qui est déchiré soit réparé, afin que vous soyez unis, d’une même pensée et d’un même dessein.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, je vous le demande au nom de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} : mettez-vous d’accord entre vous. Ne vous divisez pas en groupes. Soyez de nouveau unis, pour avoir la même façon de penser et les mêmes buts.

sw.L: Basi nawasihi, ndugu, kwa jina la Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kwamba nyote mseme jambo moja, na kusiwe na mafarakano kati yenu, bali mtengenezwe upya katika nia ile ile na katika shauri lile lile.
sw.B: Basi ndugu, nawasihi kwa jina la Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}: kubalianeni ninyi nyote, na pasiwe na migawanyiko kati yenu. Kile kilichochanika kishonwe upya, ili muungane pamoja, mkiwa na nia moja na kusudi moja.
sw.R: Ndugu, nawasihi kwa jina la Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}: kubalianeni ninyi kwa ninyi. Msigawanyike katika makundi. Unganeni tena, ili mfikiri kwa namna moja na muwe na malengo yale yale.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} ruego, hermanos, por el nombre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} que todos {{plural_you:digan|digáis}} lo mismo, y [que] no haya divisiones entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, sino [que] {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} restaurados en la misma mente y en el mismo parecer.
es.B: Hermanos, {{plural_you:les|os}} ruego por el nombre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}: {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} de acuerdo todos, y que no haya divisiones entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Que se repare lo que está roto, para que {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} unidos en un mismo pensar y un mismo propósito.
es.R: Hermanos, {{plural_you:les|os}} ruego en el nombre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}: {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} de acuerdo unos con otros. No {{plural_you:se dividan|os dividáis}} en grupos. {{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} a estar unidos, para que {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} de la misma manera y {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} los mismos propósitos.

vi.L: Vậy, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, tôi nài khuyên anh chị em bởi danh Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, là tất cả anh chị em hãy nói cùng một điều, và giữa anh chị em đừng có những sự chia rẽ, nhưng hãy được hàn gắn lại trong cùng một tâm trí và cùng một ý kiến.
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, nhân danh Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, tôi nài khuyên anh chị em: tất cả hãy đồng ý với nhau, và đừng để có sự chia rẽ giữa anh chị em. Hãy để những gì đã rách được vá lành, để anh chị em được hiệp nhất với nhau, cùng một tâm trí và cùng một mục đích.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, nhân danh Chúa chúng ta là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, tôi khuyên anh chị em: hãy đồng ý với nhau. Đừng chia ra thành từng nhóm. Hãy hiệp một trở lại, để anh chị em có cùng một cách suy nghĩ và cùng những mục tiêu.

ko.L: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 내가 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 이름으로 여러분에게 권합니다. 여러분은 모두 같은 말을 하고, 여러분 가운데 분열이 없게 하고, 같은 마음과 같은 뜻으로 [다시] 온전하게 하나가 되십시오.
ko.B: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 이름으로 여러분에게 간곡히 권합니다. 여러분은 모두 서로 뜻을 같이하고, 여러분 가운데 갈라지는 일이 없게 하십시오. 찢어진 것을 다시 꿰매듯이, 같은 생각과 같은 목적으로 굳게 하나가 되십시오.
ko.R: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 우리 주 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 이름으로 여러분에게 부탁합니다. 서로 뜻을 같이하십시오. 여러 무리로 갈라지지 마십시오. 다시 하나가 되어서 같은 생각과 같은 목표를 가지십시오.

pt.L: Ora, exorto vocês, {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, pelo nome do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}, que todos vocês digam a mesma coisa, e [que] não haja divisões entre vocês, mas [que] vocês sejam restaurados no mesmo pensamento e no mesmo parecer.
pt.B: Ora, {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, eu exorto vocês pelo nome do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}: estejam de acordo uns com os outros, todos vocês, e não deixem que haja divisões entre vocês. Que o que está rasgado seja remendado, para que vocês fiquem unidos, com um só pensamento e um só propósito.
pt.R: {{gender:Irmãos e irmãs|Irmãos}}, eu peço a vocês, em nome do nosso Senhor Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}: estejam de acordo uns com os outros. Não se dividam em grupos. Fiquem unidos de novo, para que vocês tenham o mesmo modo de pensar e os mesmos objetivos.

decisions.choice: I urge you by the name of our Lord: a strong appeal, made on the authority of Christ
alternatives: I beg you as a favor
decisions.reason: Παρακαλῶ can mean to comfort, but here it is a strong request. Paul makes it "by the name" of the Lord Jesus Christ: the appeal rests on Christ's authority, and it is the name into which they were baptized (verses 13 and 15), not the name of any teacher.

decisions.choice: say the same thing: be in agreement, with no rival parties
alternatives: hold identical opinions on every matter
decisions.reason: The phrase was used in Greek writing for parties that settle a quarrel and come to agreement. Paul is not asking for one opinion on every question; he wants an end to the rival slogans of verse 12.

decisions.choice: divisions: splits within the one church, not yet separate churches
decisions.reason: σχίσματα is a tear, as in a torn garment (Mark 2:21). The Corinthians still met together (11:18 uses the same word for divisions at their gatherings), but they were torn by rival loyalties.

decisions.choice: restored, mended: put back into good working order
decisions.reason: κατηρτισμένοι is used for mending nets (Mark 1:19) and for restoring a person who has fallen (Galatians 6:1). The picture answers the "tear" of the divisions. The perfect participle points to a settled state: mended and staying so.

decisions.choice: the same mind and the same judgment: one way of thinking and one settled purpose
decisions.reason: νοῒ is the mind, a person's way of thinking; γνώμῃ is an opinion or decision reached. Together they mean a shared outlook and a shared aim (compare Philippians 2:2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Paul writes to the whole church, women and men; Chloe's people bring the report (verse 11), and the letter speaks to women directly (7:10-16; 11:5). "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: agree with one another (B); agree with each other (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom means being in agreement (m2); Literal keeps its form.

decisions.choice: Let what is torn be mended, so that you are joined together
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of mending what is torn (m3, m4).

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} for the readers (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in English, the church is addressed as women and men together; "frères" stays available as the traditional form. Words that agree with the noun need no span.

decisions.choice: déchirures ... Que ce qui est déchiré soit réparé
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of a torn cloth mended (m3, m4), as the English does; "déchirures" prepares the image that "réparé" completes.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Romans 1:13 and Philippians 4:1, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so adding "y hermanas" would add words the Greek does not have, and the English gender setting has no Spanish span. This holds for the whole letter. For review: Chloe (verse 11) and the women of chapters 7 and 11 show that women are among those addressed, and a reviewer may prefer to make them explicit.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili needs no gender span; the only traditional alternative would add "wa kiume" (male) and change the meaning. This holds for every "ndugu" in the letter.

decisions.choice: "thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}" for the address, with the address first in the sentence (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Romans and Galatians. "Thưa" is the respectful word for addressing people; "hỡi" sounds old. Vietnamese puts an address at the head of the sentence, so Literal moves it there.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분" for the address, through the letter
decisions.reason: The address of Romans and the other letters: "여러분" is the respectful plural, and the gender setting gives "형제" as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: "권하다" (L); "간곡히 권하다" (B); "부탁하다" (R)
alternatives: "위로하다", another sense of the same Greek verb
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as a strong appeal here, not comfort.

decisions.choice: exorto
decisions.reason: "Exortar" is the written word for a strong appeal (m1); "rogar" is archaic and "pedir" too weak for Literal and Balanced. Readable says "eu peço", the everyday verb.

source.text: ἐδηλώθη γάρ μοι περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοί μου, ὑπὸ τῶν Χλόης ὅτι ἔριδες ἐν ὑμῖν εἰσιν.

records.literal_gloss: It was made clear for to me concerning you, brothers of me, by the [ones] of Chloe, that quarrels among you there are.

en.L: For it has been made clear to me about you, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, by those of Chloe, that there are quarrels among you.
en.B: I say this, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, because Chloe's people have made it clear to me that rivalries have broken out among you.
en.R: Some people from Chloe's household have told me about you, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. They say that you are arguing with each other.

fr.L: Car il m’a été clairement indiqué à votre sujet, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, par ceux de Chloé, qu’il y a des querelles parmi vous.
fr.B: Je vous dis cela, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, parce que les gens de Chloé m’ont clairement fait savoir que des rivalités ont éclaté parmi vous.
fr.R: Des personnes de la maison de Chloé m’ont parlé de vous, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}. Elles disent que vous vous disputez entre vous.

sw.L: Kwa maana nimeelezwa wazi habari zenu, ndugu zangu, na watu wa Kloe, kwamba kuna magomvi kati yenu.
sw.B: Nasema hivi, ndugu zangu, kwa sababu watu wa Kloe wameniarifu waziwazi kwamba mashindano yamezuka kati yenu.
sw.R: Watu fulani wa nyumbani mwa Kloe wameniambia habari zenu, ndugu zangu. Wanasema kwamba mnabishana ninyi kwa ninyi.

es.L: Porque se me ha hecho saber con claridad acerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hermanos míos, por los de Cloé, que hay rivalidades entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Digo esto, hermanos míos, porque la gente de Cloé me ha dejado claro que han surgido rivalidades entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Algunas personas de la casa de Cloé me han contado lo que pasa entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hermanos míos. Dicen que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} discutiendo unos con otros.

vi.L: Vì, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, những người nhà Cơ-lô-ê đã cho tôi biết rõ về anh chị em, rằng giữa anh chị em có những sự tranh cãi.
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, tôi nói điều này vì người nhà của Cơ-lô-ê đã cho tôi biết rõ rằng giữa anh chị em đã nổi lên những sự ganh đua.
vi.R: Có mấy người trong nhà bà Cơ-lô-ê đã kể cho tôi nghe về anh chị em, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi. Họ nói rằng anh chị em đang cãi nhau.

ko.L: 나의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 글로에의 [집] 사람들이 여러분에 대하여 나에게 분명히 알려 주었는데, 여러분 가운데 다툼이 있다는 것입니다.
ko.B: 나의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 내가 이렇게 말하는 것은 글로에의 집 사람들이 여러분 가운데 다툼이 일어났다고 나에게 분명히 알려 주었기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 나의 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 글로에의 집안 사람 몇이 여러분 소식을 나에게 전해 주었습니다. 여러분이 서로 다투고 있다고 합니다.

pt.L: Pois me foi informado com clareza a respeito de vocês, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, pelos [que são] de Cloe, que há contendas entre vocês.
pt.B: Digo isso, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, porque os de Cloe me deixaram claro que surgiram rivalidades entre vocês.
pt.R: Algumas pessoas da casa de Cloe me contaram sobre vocês, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}. Elas dizem que vocês estão brigando uns com os outros.

decisions.choice: Chloe's people: members of a household or business headed by a woman named Chloe
decisions.reason: τῶν Χλόης is "those of Chloe", with no noun. The phrase usually means members of someone's household: family, slaves or freed slaves, or agents traveling on business. Chloe is not mentioned anywhere else. She may have lived in Corinth or in Ephesus, where Paul was writing (16:8); the Corinthians clearly knew who she was. Women such as Lydia (Acts 16:14-15) headed households among the first believers.

decisions.choice: quarrels: rivalries and arguments
decisions.reason: ἔριδες is strife or rivalry, a word Paul lists among the works of the flesh (Galatians 5:20) and uses of the Corinthians again in 3:3. It names the wrangling behind the slogans of verse 12.

decisions.choice: made clear: a definite report from people Paul names, not rumor
decisions.reason: ἐδηλώθη means shown or made plain. Paul names his source openly, so the church knows the report is not gossip.

decisions.choice: my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 10: the letter is written to women and men.

decisions.choice: Chloe's people (B); some people from Chloe's household (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase has no noun (m1). Balanced keeps it open; Readable says what it usually meant.

decisions.choice: I say this ... because
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out how "for" links the report to the appeal of verse 10.

decisions.choice: "bà Cơ-lô-ê" (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese names a respected woman with "bà"; Chloe headed a household (m1).

decisions.choice: "글로에", "그리스보", "가이오", "스데바나", "아볼로", "소스데네", "고린도", "아가야" in their Protestant Korean forms; "게바" (L, B) and "베드로" (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide asks for the established Protestant forms of names. Cephas is "게바" at Literal and Balanced, as in John 1:42 and Galatians, and "베드로" at Readable, as the English does.

decisions.choice: os de Cloe
decisions.reason: Portuguese can say "os de Cloe" with no noun, as the Greek does, and so leave open who they were (m1). "A família de Cloe" would be too narrow.

source.text: λέγω δὲ τοῦτο ὅτι ἕκαστος ὑμῶν λέγει· Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου, Ἐγὼ δὲ Ἀπολλῶ, Ἐγὼ δὲ Κηφᾶ, Ἐγὼ δὲ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: I mean but this, that each of you says, I on the one hand am of Paul, I but of Apollos, I but of Cephas, I but of Christ.

en.L: Now I mean this, that each of you says, "I am of Paul," "But I of Apollos," "But I of Cephas," "But I of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}."
en.B: What I mean is that every one of you takes a side: "I am for Paul," "I am for Apollos," "I am for Cephas," "I am for {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}."
en.R: Here is what I mean. Each of you is taking sides. One says, "I am on Paul's side." Another says, "I am on Apollos's side." Another says, "I am on Peter's side." And another says, "I am on {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}'s side."

fr.L: Or je veux dire ceci, que chacun de vous dit : « Moi, je suis de Paul », « Et moi, d’Apollos », « Et moi, de Céphas », « Et moi, du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ».
fr.B: Ce que je veux dire, c’est que chacun de vous prend parti : « Moi, je suis pour Paul », « Moi, je suis pour Apollos », « Moi, je suis pour Céphas », « Moi, je suis pour le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ».
fr.R: Voici ce que je veux dire. Chacun de vous prend parti. L’un dit : « Moi, je suis du côté de Paul. » Un autre dit : « Moi, je suis du côté d’Apollos. » Un autre dit : « Moi, je suis du côté de Pierre. » Et un autre encore dit : « Moi, je suis du côté du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. »

sw.L: Basi ninamaanisha hivi, kwamba kila mmoja wenu anasema, "Mimi ni wa Paulo," "Lakini mimi [ni] wa Apolo," "Lakini mimi [ni] wa Kefa," "Lakini mimi [ni] wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}."
sw.B: Ninachomaanisha ni kwamba kila mmoja wenu anashika upande: "Mimi ni mfuasi wa Paulo," "Mimi ni mfuasi wa Apolo," "Mimi ni mfuasi wa Kefa," "Mimi ni mfuasi wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}."
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo ninavyomaanisha. Kila mmoja wenu anachagua upande. Mmoja anasema, "Mimi niko upande wa Paulo." Mwingine anasema, "Mimi niko upande wa Apolo." Mwingine anasema, "Mimi niko upande wa Petro." Na mwingine anasema, "Mimi niko upande wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}."

es.L: Quiero decir esto: que cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} dice: «Yo soy de Pablo», «Y yo de Apolos», «Y yo de Cefas», «Y yo de {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}».
es.B: Lo que quiero decir es que cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} toma partido: «Yo estoy con Pablo», «Yo estoy con Apolos», «Yo estoy con Cefas», «Yo estoy con {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}».
es.R: Esto es lo que quiero decir: cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se ha puesto de un lado. Uno dice: «Yo estoy del lado de Pablo». Otro dice: «Yo estoy del lado de Apolos». Otro: «Yo estoy del lado de Pedro». Y otro: «Yo estoy del lado {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}».

vi.L: Tôi muốn nói điều này: mỗi người trong anh chị em nói: "Tôi thuộc về Phao-lô," "Còn tôi thuộc về A-bô-lô," "Còn tôi thuộc về Sê-pha," "Còn tôi thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}."
