pt.R: Deus mostrou que a sabedoria do mundo é loucura.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer "yes"
decisions.reason: οὐχὶ marks a question that expects agreement: yes, God has done this.

decisions.choice: made foolish: exposed as foolish, shown to be folly by what God has done in the cross
decisions.reason: ἐμώρανεν means to make foolish. God has not argued the world's wisdom down; by saving people through a crucified Messiah he has shown that it could not find him (verse 21; compare Isaiah 44:25).

decisions.choice: the world: human society and its ways of thinking, apart from God
decisions.reason: κόσμου here means humankind as it thinks and lives without God, as in verses 21 and 27-28.

decisions.choice: God has shown that ...
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes" (m1); Readable gives the answer as a plain statement.

decisions.choice: shown ... to be foolishness
decisions.reason: Balanced says how God made it foolish (m2) and keeps the word "foolishness" (see verse 18).

source.text: ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἐν τῇ σοφίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἔγνω ὁ κόσμος διὰ τῆς σοφίας τὸν θεόν, εὐδόκησεν ὁ θεὸς διὰ τῆς μωρίας τοῦ κηρύγματος σῶσαι τοὺς πιστεύοντας.

records.literal_gloss: Since for in the wisdom of the God not knew the world through the wisdom the God, was pleased the God through the foolishness of the preaching to save the [ones] believing.

en.L: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through [its] wisdom, God was pleased through the foolishness of the preaching to save those who believe.
en.B: For in God's wisdom the world, with all its wisdom, did not come to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So it was God's good pleasure to save those who believe through the message we preach, foolishness though it seems.
en.R: God in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wisdom made sure that the world would not come to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by its own wisdom. Instead, God decided to save those who believe through the message we preach, a message that sounds foolish.

fr.L: Car puisque, dans la sagesse de Dieu, le monde n’a pas connu Dieu par [sa] sagesse, Dieu a trouvé bon, par la folie de la prédication, de sauver ceux qui croient.
fr.B: Car, dans la sagesse de Dieu, le monde, avec toute sa sagesse, n’est pas parvenu à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaître. Alors Dieu a trouvé bon de sauver ceux qui croient par le message que nous proclamons, ce message qui passe pour une folie.
fr.R: Dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sagesse, Dieu a fait en sorte que le monde ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} connaisse pas par sa propre sagesse. Au lieu de cela, Dieu a décidé de sauver ceux qui croient grâce au message que nous annonçons, un message qui paraît une folie.

sw.L: Kwa maana, kwa kuwa katika hekima ya Mungu ulimwengu haukumjua Mungu kupitia hekima [yake], Mungu alipendezwa kupitia upumbavu wa mahubiri kuwaokoa wale wanaoamini.
sw.B: Kwa maana katika hekima ya Mungu, ulimwengu, pamoja na hekima yake yote, haukufikia kumjua Mungu. Kwa hiyo Mungu alipenda kuwaokoa wanaoamini kupitia ujumbe tunaouhubiri, ingawa unaonekana kuwa upumbavu.
sw.R: Mungu kwa hekima {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} alihakikisha kwamba ulimwengu usimjue kwa hekima yake wenyewe. Badala yake, Mungu aliamua kuwaokoa wale wanaoamini kupitia ujumbe tunaouhubiri, ujumbe unaosikika kama upumbavu.

es.L: Porque ya que, en la sabiduría de Dios, el mundo no conoció a Dios por medio de [su] sabiduría, a Dios le agradó salvar a los que creen por medio de la necedad de la predicación.
es.B: Pues, en la sabiduría de Dios, el mundo, con toda su sabiduría, no llegó a conocerlo. Por eso Dios tuvo a bien salvar a los que creen por medio del mensaje que predicamos, aunque parezca necedad.
es.R: Dios, en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} sabiduría, dispuso que el mundo no llegara a conocerlo por su propia sabiduría. En cambio, Dios decidió salvar a los que creen por medio del mensaje que predicamos, un mensaje que parece una tontería.

vi.L: Vì bởi trong sự khôn ngoan của Đức Chúa Trời, thế gian đã không nhận biết Đức Chúa Trời qua sự khôn ngoan [của mình], nên Đức Chúa Trời đã vui lòng dùng sự dại dột của sự rao giảng để cứu những người tin.
vi.B: Vì trong sự khôn ngoan của Đức Chúa Trời, thế gian dù có mọi sự khôn ngoan của mình vẫn không nhận biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vì vậy, Đức Chúa Trời đã vui lòng cứu những người tin qua sứ điệp chúng tôi rao giảng, dù sứ điệp ấy có vẻ dại dột.
vi.R: Trong sự khôn ngoan của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, Đức Chúa Trời đã định rằng thế gian sẽ không thể nhờ sự khôn ngoan của mình mà biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Thay vào đó, Đức Chúa Trời đã quyết định cứu những người tin qua sứ điệp chúng tôi rao giảng, một sứ điệp nghe có vẻ dại dột.

ko.L: 하나님의 지혜 안에서 세상은 [자기] 지혜를 통하여 하나님을 알지 못했으므로, 하나님께서는 전도의 어리석음을 통하여 믿는 사람들을 구원하기를 기뻐하셨습니다.
ko.B: 하나님의 지혜로 말미암아 세상은 그 모든 지혜로도 하나님을 알지 못했습니다. 그래서 하나님께서는 우리가 전하는 메시지, 어리석어 보이는 그 메시지를 통해 믿는 사람들을 구원하시기를 기뻐하셨습니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 그분의 지혜로, 세상이 자기 지혜로는 그분을 알 수 없게 하셨습니다. 그 대신 하나님께서는 우리가 전하는 소식을 통해 믿는 사람들을 구원하기로 하셨습니다. 그 소식은 어리석게 들리는 소식입니다.

pt.L: Pois, visto que, na sabedoria de Deus, o mundo não conheceu a Deus por meio da [sua] sabedoria, agradou a Deus, por meio da loucura da pregação, salvar os que creem.
pt.B: Pois, na sabedoria de Deus, o mundo, com toda a sua sabedoria, não chegou a conhecê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}. Por isso foi do agrado de Deus salvar os que creem por meio da mensagem que pregamos, ainda que ela pareça loucura.
pt.R: Deus, na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} sabedoria, fez com que o mundo não chegasse a conhecê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} pela sua própria sabedoria. Em vez disso, Deus decidiu salvar os que acreditam por meio da mensagem que pregamos, uma mensagem que parece loucura.

decisions.choice: in the wisdom of God: by God's wise purpose it came about that the world did not know him through its own wisdom
alternatives: though surrounded by the signs of God's wisdom in creation, the world failed to know him (compare Romans 1:19-21)
decisions.reason: σοφίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ may describe God's wise plan, which allowed human wisdom to fail so that salvation would come as a gift; or the wisdom God showed in creation, which the world saw and still did not know him. The first fits Paul's point here, that God has made the world's wisdom foolish (verse 20); the second fits Romans 1. Both say that human wisdom could not reach God.

decisions.choice: through its wisdom: human wisdom, as a way to God, failed
decisions.reason: The article in τῆς σοφίας points to the world's own wisdom, just mentioned in verse 20. The world did not lack cleverness, but cleverness did not lead it to know God.

decisions.choice: the preaching: the message proclaimed, Christ crucified, not the act or style of preaching
alternatives: the foolish act of preaching itself
decisions.reason: κηρύγματος names what a herald announces. What seems foolish is the content, a crucified Messiah (verse 23), not the speaking.

decisions.choice: was pleased: chose freely, as his good purpose
decisions.reason: εὐδόκησεν is used of God's free decision (Galatians 1:15; Colossians 1:19). Saving people through this message was God's chosen way, not an accident.

decisions.choice: the message we preach, foolishness though it seems (B); a message that sounds foolish (R)
decisions.reason: Paul calls the message "foolishness" with irony: it is what the world counts foolish (verses 18 and 25). Balanced and Readable make the irony clear; Literal keeps his phrase.

decisions.choice: God in his wisdom made sure that
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m1.

decisions.choice: conocerlo, no deity_pronoun span
alternatives: a Él no llegó a conocer, with a span
decisions.reason: Where the pronoun for God is joined to the end of the verb ("conocerlo"), Spanish writes it as part of the word, and a capital inside a word is not used, so it takes no deity_pronoun span. Free and preceding pronouns ("{{deity_pronoun:su|Su}}", "{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ...") keep the span throughout the letter.

decisions.choice: "전도" (L); "우리가 전하는 메시지" (B); "우리가 전하는 소식" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as the message proclaimed, not the act or style of preaching, so Balanced and Readable name the message; "메시지" is the current word for a message preached, here and in verse 18 (B).

decisions.choice: os que creem (L, B); os que acreditam (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as the style guide sets it: "crer" at Literal and Balanced, the written word that keeps its link with "a fé"; Readable says "acreditar", the everyday verb.

source.text: ἐπειδὴ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι σημεῖα αἰτοῦσιν καὶ Ἕλληνες σοφίαν ζητοῦσιν·

records.literal_gloss: Since both Jews signs ask and Greeks wisdom seek;

en.L: For Jews ask for signs, and Greeks seek wisdom.
en.B: Jews ask for signs, and Greeks look for wisdom.
en.R: Jewish people ask for signs, acts of power that prove God is at work. Greeks want wisdom that makes sense to them.

fr.L: Car les Juifs demandent des signes, et les Grecs cherchent la sagesse.
fr.B: Les Juifs demandent des signes, et les Grecs recherchent la sagesse.
fr.R: Les Juifs demandent des signes, des actes de puissance qui prouvent que Dieu agit. Les Grecs veulent une sagesse qui leur paraisse raisonnable.

sw.L: Kwa maana Wayahudi wanaomba ishara, na Wagiriki wanatafuta hekima.
sw.B: Wayahudi wanadai ishara, na Wagiriki wanatafuta hekima.
sw.R: Wayahudi wanataka ishara, yaani matendo ya nguvu yanayothibitisha kwamba Mungu yuko kazini. Wagiriki wanataka hekima inayoeleweka kwa akili zao.

es.L: Porque los judíos piden señales, y los griegos buscan sabiduría.
es.B: Los judíos piden señales, y los griegos buscan sabiduría.
es.R: Los judíos piden señales, es decir, actos de poder que prueben que Dios está obrando. Los griegos quieren una sabiduría que tenga sentido para ellos.

vi.L: Vì người Do Thái đòi dấu lạ, còn người Hy Lạp tìm kiếm sự khôn ngoan.
vi.B: Người Do Thái đòi dấu lạ, còn người Hy Lạp tìm sự khôn ngoan.
vi.R: Người Do Thái đòi xem dấu lạ, là những việc quyền năng chứng tỏ Đức Chúa Trời đang hành động. Người Hy Lạp muốn có sự khôn ngoan mà họ thấy là hợp lý.

ko.L: 유대인들은 표적을 구하고, 그리스 사람들은 지혜를 찾습니다.
ko.B: 유대인들은 표적을 요구하고, 그리스 사람들은 지혜를 찾습니다.
ko.R: 유대인들은 표적, 곧 하나님께서 일하고 계시다는 것을 보여 주는 능력 있는 일을 보여 달라고 합니다. 그리스 사람들은 자기들이 이해할 수 있는 지혜를 원합니다.

pt.L: Pois tanto os judeus pedem sinais como os gregos buscam sabedoria.
pt.B: Os judeus pedem sinais, e os gregos procuram sabedoria.
pt.R: Os judeus pedem sinais, atos de poder que provem que Deus está agindo. Os gregos querem uma sabedoria que faça sentido para eles.

decisions.choice: since indeed: a further reason, which leads into verse 23 ("but we preach")
alternatives: a clause that depends on verse 23: "Since Jews ask ..., we preach"
decisions.reason: ἐπειδὴ καὶ ("since also") picks up the reasoning of verse 21. The SBLGNT ends the verse with a raised dot, so the clause stands on its own and every level renders it as a statement; verse 23 then answers it with "but we".

decisions.choice: signs: acts of power that would prove God was behind a message
decisions.reason: Jews looked for God to act with power, as he had at the Exodus, and asked Jesus for σημεῖα (Mark 8:11; John 6:30). A Messiah who died in weakness gave them none.

decisions.choice: Greeks: people of Greek language and culture, standing here for non-Jews in general
decisions.reason: Ἕλληνες were known for philosophy and the love of argument. In verse 23 Paul uses the word "Gentiles" for the same group, and in verse 24 "Greeks" again.

decisions.choice: signs, acts of power that prove God is at work; wisdom that makes sense to them
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of sign and what kind of wisdom each group wanted (m2, m3).

decisions.choice: "dấu lạ" for semeia
decisions.reason: "Dấu lạ" is the style guide's word for a sign, kept apart from "phép lạ" (miracle); Readable explains what kind of sign was asked for, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "표적" for signs; "그리스 사람" for Greeks, at every level
decisions.reason: "표적" is the word of John and the Gospels for a sign that points to God at work, never "기적" (miracle). "그리스 사람" is the current name, as in Romans 1:14; "헬라인" is the older church word.

source.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ κηρύσσομεν Χριστὸν ἐσταυρωμένον, Ἰουδαίοις μὲν σκάνδαλον ἔθνεσιν δὲ μωρίαν, αὐτοῖς δὲ τοῖς κλητοῖς, Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν, Χριστὸν θεοῦ δύναμιν καὶ θεοῦ σοφίαν.

records.literal_gloss: We but preach Christ having been crucified, to Jews on one hand stumbling block, to Gentiles but foolishness, \v 24 to them but the called [ones], Jews both and Greeks, Christ of God power and of God wisdom.

en.L: But we preach {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} crucified, to Jews a stumbling block and to Gentiles foolishness, \v 24 but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [the] power of God and [the] wisdom of God.
en.B: But we proclaim {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} crucified. To Jews this is an offense they stumble over, and to Gentiles it is foolishness, \v 24 but to those whom God has called, Jews and Greeks alike, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is God's power and God's wisdom.
en.R: But we tell people about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, who died on a cross. Jewish people are offended by this message, and other people think it is foolish. \v 24 But God has called some people, both Jews and Greeks. To them {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is the power of God and the wisdom of God.

fr.L: Mais nous, nous prêchons le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} crucifié, pour les Juifs une pierre d’achoppement et pour les nations une folie, \v 24 mais pour ceux qui sont appelés, Juifs aussi bien que Grecs, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, puissance de Dieu et sagesse de Dieu.
fr.B: Mais nous, nous proclamons le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} crucifié. Pour les Juifs, c’est un scandale sur lequel ils trébuchent, et pour les non-Juifs, c’est une folie ; \v 24 mais pour ceux que Dieu a appelés, Juifs comme Grecs, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est la puissance de Dieu et la sagesse de Dieu.
fr.R: Mais nous, nous parlons aux gens du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, qui est mort sur une croix. Les Juifs sont choqués par ce message, et les autres peuples pensent que c’est une folie. \v 24 Mais Dieu a appelé certaines personnes, des Juifs comme des Grecs. Pour elles, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est la puissance de Dieu et la sagesse de Dieu.

sw.L: Lakini sisi tunamhubiri {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} aliyesulubiwa, kwa Wayahudi kikwazo na kwa watu wa mataifa upumbavu, \v 24 lakini kwa wale walioitwa wenyewe, Wayahudi na Wagiriki pia, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} [ni] nguvu ya Mungu na hekima ya Mungu.
sw.B: Lakini sisi tunamhubiri {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} aliyesulubiwa. Kwa Wayahudi hili ni kikwazo kinachowakwaza, na kwa watu wa mataifa ni upumbavu; \v 24 lakini kwa wale ambao Mungu amewaita, Wayahudi na Wagiriki vilevile, {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni nguvu ya Mungu na hekima ya Mungu.
sw.R: Lakini sisi tunawaambia watu habari za {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, aliyekufa msalabani. Wayahudi wanachukizwa na ujumbe huu, na watu wengine wanaona ni upumbavu. \v 24 Lakini Mungu amewaita baadhi ya watu, Wayahudi na Wagiriki pia. Kwao {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni nguvu ya Mungu na hekima ya Mungu.

es.L: Pero nosotros predicamos a {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} crucificado, para [los] judíos piedra de tropiezo y para [los] gentiles necedad, \v 24 pero para los llamados mismos, tanto judíos como griegos, {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} [es] poder de Dios y sabiduría de Dios.
es.B: Pero nosotros proclamamos {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} crucificado. Para los judíos es una ofensa con la que tropiezan, y para los gentiles es necedad; \v 24 pero para los que Dios ha llamado, judíos y griegos por igual, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} es el poder de Dios y la sabiduría de Dios.
es.R: Pero nosotros anunciamos {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, que murió en una cruz. A los judíos les ofende este mensaje, y los demás piensan que es una tontería. \v 24 Pero Dios ha llamado a algunos, tanto judíos como griegos. Para ellos, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} es el poder de Dios y la sabiduría de Dios.

vi.L: Nhưng chúng tôi rao giảng {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đã bị đóng đinh trên thập tự giá, đối với người Do Thái là vật gây vấp ngã, còn đối với dân ngoại là sự dại dột, \v 24 nhưng đối với chính những người được kêu gọi, cả người Do Thái lẫn người Hy Lạp, thì {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} là quyền năng của Đức Chúa Trời và sự khôn ngoan của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Nhưng chúng tôi rao giảng {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} chịu đóng đinh trên thập tự giá. Đối với người Do Thái, đó là điều xúc phạm khiến họ vấp ngã, còn đối với dân ngoại, đó là sự dại dột. \v 24 Nhưng đối với những người được Đức Chúa Trời kêu gọi, dù là người Do Thái hay người Hy Lạp, {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} là quyền năng của Đức Chúa Trời và sự khôn ngoan của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Nhưng chúng tôi nói cho người ta biết về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, là Đấng đã chết trên thập tự giá. Người Do Thái thấy sứ điệp này thật xúc phạm, còn những người khác thì cho là dại dột. \v 24 Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời đã kêu gọi một số người, cả người Do Thái lẫn người Hy Lạp. Đối với họ, {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} là quyền năng của Đức Chúa Trời và là sự khôn ngoan của Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그러나 우리는 십자가에 못 박히신 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 전합니다. [그것은] 유대인들에게는 걸림돌이요 이방 사람들에게는 어리석음이지만, \v 24 부르심을 받은 사람들에게는 유대인이든 그리스 사람이든 하나님의 능력이며 하나님의 지혜이신 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 우리는 십자가에 못 박히신 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 선포합니다. 이것은 유대인들에게는 걸려 넘어지게 하는 거리끼는 것이고, 이방 사람들에게는 어리석은 것입니다. \v 24 그러나 하나님께서 부르신 사람들에게는, 유대인이든 그리스 사람이든, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 하나님의 능력이시며 하나님의 지혜이십니다.
ko.R: 그러나 우리는 십자가에서 죽으신 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}에 대해 사람들에게 전합니다. 유대인들은 이 소식에 기분이 상하고, 다른 사람들은 이 소식을 어리석다고 생각합니다. \v 24 그러나 하나님께서는 어떤 사람들을 부르셨습니다. 유대인도 있고 그리스 사람도 있습니다. 그 사람들에게 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 하나님의 능력이시고 하나님의 지혜이십니다.

pt.L: Mas nós pregamos {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} crucificado, para judeus pedra de tropeço, e para [as] nações loucura, \v 24 mas para os próprios chamados, tanto judeus como gregos, {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, poder de Deus e sabedoria de Deus.
pt.B: Mas nós anunciamos {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} crucificado. Para os judeus, isso é uma ofensa em que eles tropeçam, e para os não judeus é loucura; \v 24 mas para aqueles a quem Deus chamou, judeus e gregos, {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} é o poder de Deus e a sabedoria de Deus.
pt.R: Mas nós falamos às pessoas sobre {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}, que morreu na cruz. Os judeus se ofendem com essa mensagem, e as outras pessoas acham que ela é loucura. \v 24 Mas Deus chamou algumas pessoas, tanto judeus como gregos. Para elas, {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} é o poder de Deus e a sabedoria de Deus.

decisions.choice: Christ crucified: the Messiah who was crucified, and who remains the crucified one
decisions.reason: ἐσταυρωμένον is a perfect participle: the crucified one is what he is, even as the risen Lord (2:2; Galatians 3:1). To Jews a crucified Messiah was a contradiction: the Messiah was to triumph, and the Law says that anyone hanged on a tree is under God's curse (Deuteronomy 21:22-23; Galatians 3:13).

decisions.choice: stumbling block: something that trips people up and gives deep offense
decisions.reason: σκάνδαλον is the trigger of a trap, then anything that makes someone fall. Paul uses it of Christ in Romans 9:33, echoing Isaiah 8:14. Jews looking for signs of power tripped over a Messiah who died in weakness.

decisions.choice: the called: those God has called, who see in the same crucified Christ God's power and wisdom
decisions.reason: κλητοῖς picks up the call of verses 1, 2, 9 and 26: God's call that brings people to faith. The second Χριστὸν repeats the object of "we preach": the same message that offends others is, to the called, God's power and wisdom.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "to Gentiles"
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts read "to Greeks", matching verses 22 and 24; the early manuscripts have "Gentiles". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. The title setting matters here: a crucified Messiah was the offense (m1).

decisions.choice: an offense they stumble over (B); are offended (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps both the picture and the sense (m2); Readable gives the sense.

decisions.choice: other people
decisions.reason: "Gentiles" is church language for non-Jews; Readable uses plain words.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); les autres peuples (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in the style guide: "les païens" today suggests people with no religion and a judgment, and "les Gentils" is no longer current French. Readable follows the English "other people".

decisions.choice: une pierre d'achoppement (L); un scandale sur lequel ils trébuchent (B)
decisions.reason: French "scandale" comes from this word but now means public outrage; Literal keeps the picture of a stone that trips people up, and Balanced joins the familiar word to the picture (m2), as the English "an offense they stumble over" does.

decisions.choice: watu wa mataifa
decisions.reason: "Watu wa mataifa" is the phrase settled in Swahili Romans for the Gentiles; "wapagani" (pagans) would add a judgment the Greek word does not carry.

decisions.choice: "dân ngoại" (L, B); "những người khác" (R) for ethnesin; "người Hy Lạp" at every level for Hellenes
decisions.reason: "Dân ngoại" is the word of the Vietnamese Romans and Galatians for the Gentiles; Readable follows the English "other people". The Greeks are named as Greeks at every level, as the English does, since here they stand for the cultured non-Jewish world (m3 in verse 22).

decisions.choice: "vật gây vấp ngã" (L); "điều xúc phạm khiến họ vấp ngã" (B) for skandalon
decisions.reason: "Vấp ngã" keeps the picture of tripping, as the Vietnamese Romans does for this word family (16:17); Balanced adds the offense, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "걸림돌" (L); "걸려 넘어지게 하는 거리끼는 것" (B); "기분이 상하다" (R); "이방 사람들" (L, B) and "다른 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: "걸림돌" is the word of Romans 9:33 and 14:13; Balanced spells out that it trips people and offends them. "이방 사람들" is the word of Romans for the Gentiles; Readable here follows the English "other people".

decisions.choice: as nações (L); os não judeus (B); as outras pessoas (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as the style guide sets it: where the English says "Gentiles", Balanced says "os não judeus" (no hyphen, 1990 spelling) and Literal "as nações", the word's form; "gentios" is church language. Readable follows the English "other people".

decisions.choice: pedra de tropeço (L); uma ofensa em que eles tropeçam (B)
decisions.reason: "Escândalo" is the Greek word's Portuguese descendant, but today it means a public outrage or a piece of gossip; "pedra de tropeço" keeps the picture of something that makes people fall (m2), the sense docs/corinthians-terms.md keeps for this word family.

source.text: ὅτι τὸ μωρὸν τοῦ θεοῦ σοφώτερον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐστίν, καὶ τὸ ἀσθενὲς τοῦ θεοῦ ἰσχυρότερον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: Because the foolish [thing] of the God wiser than the humans is, and the weak [thing] of the God stronger than the humans.

en.L: Because the foolish [thing] of God is wiser than humans, and the weak [thing] of God [is] stronger than humans.
en.B: For the foolish thing God has done is wiser than any human wisdom, and the weak thing God has done is stronger than any human strength.
en.R: What looks like foolishness from God is wiser than all human wisdom. What looks like weakness from God is stronger than all human strength.

fr.L: Parce que ce qui est fou de la part de Dieu est plus sage que les humains, et ce qui est faible de la part de Dieu [est] plus fort que les humains.
fr.B: Car ce que Dieu a fait de fou est plus sage que toute la sagesse humaine, et ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait de faible est plus fort que toute la force humaine.
fr.R: Ce qui ressemble à de la folie de la part de Dieu est plus sage que toute la sagesse humaine. Ce qui ressemble à de la faiblesse de la part de Dieu est plus fort que toute la force humaine.

sw.L: Kwa sababu kile cha Mungu kilicho upumbavu kina hekima kuliko wanadamu, na kile cha Mungu kilicho dhaifu kina nguvu kuliko wanadamu.
sw.B: Kwa maana jambo la kipumbavu alilofanya Mungu lina hekima kuliko hekima yoyote ya wanadamu, na jambo dhaifu alilofanya Mungu lina nguvu kuliko nguvu yoyote ya wanadamu.
sw.R: Kile kinachoonekana kuwa upumbavu wa Mungu kina hekima kuliko hekima yote ya wanadamu. Kile kinachoonekana kuwa udhaifu wa Mungu kina nguvu kuliko nguvu zote za wanadamu.

es.L: Porque lo necio de Dios es más sabio que los seres humanos, y lo débil de Dios [es] más fuerte que los seres humanos.
es.B: Porque lo necio que Dios ha hecho es más sabio que toda sabiduría humana, y lo débil que Dios ha hecho es más fuerte que toda fuerza humana.
es.R: Lo que de parte de Dios parece una tontería es más sabio que toda la sabiduría humana. Lo que de parte de Dios parece debilidad es más fuerte que toda la fuerza humana.

vi.L: Vì sự dại dột của Đức Chúa Trời thì khôn ngoan hơn loài người, và sự yếu đuối của Đức Chúa Trời thì mạnh mẽ hơn loài người.
vi.B: Vì điều dại dột Đức Chúa Trời đã làm còn khôn ngoan hơn mọi sự khôn ngoan của loài người, và điều yếu đuối Đức Chúa Trời đã làm còn mạnh mẽ hơn mọi sức mạnh của loài người.
vi.R: Điều trông như dại dột từ Đức Chúa Trời lại khôn ngoan hơn tất cả sự khôn ngoan của loài người. Điều trông như yếu đuối từ Đức Chúa Trời lại mạnh mẽ hơn tất cả sức mạnh của loài người.

ko.L: 하나님의 어리석음이 사람들보다 지혜롭고, 하나님의 약함이 사람들보다 강하기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 하신 어리석어 보이는 일이 사람의 어떤 지혜보다 지혜롭고, 하나님께서 하신 약해 보이는 일이 사람의 어떤 힘보다 강하기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 하신 일이 어리석어 보여도 그것은 사람의 모든 지혜보다 더 지혜롭습니다. 하나님께서 하신 일이 약해 보여도 그것은 사람의 모든 힘보다 더 강합니다.

pt.L: Porque a [coisa] louca de Deus é mais sábia que os seres humanos, e a [coisa] fraca de Deus [é] mais forte que os seres humanos.
pt.B: Pois aquilo que Deus fez e parece loucura é mais sábio que qualquer sabedoria humana, e aquilo que Deus fez e parece fraqueza é mais forte que qualquer força humana.
pt.R: As coisas de Deus que parecem loucura são mais sábias do que toda a sabedoria humana. As coisas de Deus que parecem fraqueza são mais fortes do que toda a força humana.

decisions.choice: the foolish thing of God: what God has done that seems foolish and weak, the cross
alternatives: foolishness and weakness as qualities in God
decisions.reason: μωρὸν and ἀσθενὲς are neuter adjectives with the article: "the foolish thing", "the weak thing". Paul is not saying God is foolish or weak, but that what God has done in a crucified Messiah, which looks foolish and weak, outdoes everything human beings can do (2 Corinthians 13:4).

decisions.choice: wiser than humans: wiser than humans are, wiser than all their wisdom
decisions.reason: The comparison is short: σοφώτερον τῶν ἀνθρώπων is "wiser than humans", meaning wiser than human wisdom; likewise with strength. The shorthand makes the point bluntly.

decisions.choice: the foolish thing God has done; any human wisdom (B); what looks like foolishness from God; all human wisdom (R)
alternatives: the foolishness of God is wiser than men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what "the foolish thing of God" refers to (m1) and complete the comparison (m2). Literal keeps "humans", which is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: los seres humanos
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings of either sex, and Spanish "los hombres" is often heard as men only, so Literal says "los seres humanos", as the English Literal says "humans" without a setting.

decisions.choice: "하나님의 어리석음 ... 하나님의 약함" (L)
decisions.reason: Korean nouns stand in for the Greek "the foolish [thing]" without brackets; the meaning decision says what is meant, the cross, and Balanced and Readable say "what God has done".

decisions.choice: aquilo que Deus fez e parece loucura ... parece fraqueza
alternatives: o que Deus fez de louco
decisions.reason: "A loucura de Deus" would say in Portuguese that God is out of his mind. Balanced adds "parece", which keeps the irony m1 describes: what God did looks foolish and weak, and is not.

source.text: Βλέπετε γὰρ τὴν κλῆσιν ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι οὐ πολλοὶ σοφοὶ κατὰ σάρκα, οὐ πολλοὶ δυνατοί, οὐ πολλοὶ εὐγενεῖς·

records.literal_gloss: Look at for the calling of you, brothers, that not many wise according to flesh, not many powerful, not many well-born;

en.L: For consider your calling, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}: not many [were] wise according to [the] flesh, not many powerful, not many well-born.
en.B: Just look at your own calling, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. When God called you, not many of you were wise as people measure wisdom, not many held power, not many came from leading families.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, think about who you were when God called you. Not many of you were wise in the eyes of other people. Not many of you were important or powerful. Not many came from important families.

fr.L: Considérez en effet votre appel, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} : [il n’y avait] pas beaucoup de sages selon la chair, pas beaucoup de puissants, pas beaucoup de gens bien nés.
fr.B: Considérez donc votre propre appel, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}. Quand Dieu vous a appelés, peu d’entre vous étaient sages selon les critères humains, peu avaient du pouvoir, peu venaient de grandes familles.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, pensez à ce que vous étiez quand Dieu vous a appelés. Peu d’entre vous étaient sages aux yeux des autres. Peu d’entre vous étaient importants ou puissants. Peu venaient de familles connues.

sw.L: Kwa maana angalieni wito wenu, ndugu: si wengi [mliokuwa] wenye hekima kwa kadiri ya mwili, si wengi wenye nguvu, si wengi wa ukoo bora.
sw.B: Angalieni wito wenu wenyewe, ndugu. Mungu alipowaita, si wengi wenu mliokuwa na hekima kwa vipimo vya kibinadamu, si wengi mliokuwa na mamlaka, si wengi mliotoka katika familia mashuhuri.
sw.R: Ndugu, fikirini mlivyokuwa wakati Mungu alipowaita. Si wengi wenu mliokuwa na hekima machoni pa watu wengine. Si wengi mliokuwa watu muhimu au wenye nguvu. Si wengi mliotoka katika familia za heshima.

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} llamamiento, hermanos: no muchos [eran] sabios según [la] carne, no muchos poderosos, no muchos de noble cuna.
es.B: {{plural_you:Fíjense|Fijaos}} en cómo {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} llamados, hermanos. Cuando Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó, no muchos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} eran sabios según los criterios humanos, no muchos tenían poder, no muchos venían de familias importantes.
es.R: Hermanos, {{plural_you:piensen|pensad}} en quiénes {{plural_you:eran|erais}} cuando Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} llamó. No muchos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} eran sabios a los ojos de la gente. No muchos eran importantes o poderosos. No muchos venían de familias importantes.

vi.L: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, vì hãy xem sự kêu gọi của anh chị em: không có nhiều người khôn ngoan theo xác thịt, không có nhiều người quyền thế, không có nhiều người dòng dõi cao sang.
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, hãy nhìn lại sự kêu gọi của chính anh chị em. Khi Đức Chúa Trời kêu gọi anh chị em, trong anh chị em không có nhiều người khôn ngoan theo cách người đời đánh giá, không có nhiều người nắm quyền thế, không có nhiều người xuất thân từ gia đình danh giá.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, hãy nghĩ xem anh chị em là ai khi Đức Chúa Trời gọi anh chị em. Không có nhiều người trong anh chị em là người khôn ngoan trong mắt người khác. Không có nhiều người quan trọng hay có quyền thế. Không có nhiều người xuất thân từ gia đình quyền quý.

ko.L: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분의 부르심을 보십시오. 육신을 따라 지혜로운 사람이 많지 않고, 권력 있는 사람이 많지 않고, 가문 좋은 사람이 많지 않습니다.
ko.B: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 여러분이 부르심을 받을 때를 생각해 보십시오. 사람의 기준으로 지혜로운 사람이 많지 않았고, 권력을 가진 사람도 많지 않았고, 명문가 출신도 많지 않았습니다.
ko.R: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 하나님께서 여러분을 부르셨을 때 여러분이 어떤 사람이었는지 생각해 보십시오. 다른 사람들이 보기에 지혜로운 사람은 많지 않았습니다. 중요하거나 힘 있는 사람도 많지 않았습니다. 이름난 집안 출신도 많지 않았습니다.

pt.L: Pois vejam o chamado de vocês, {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}: não muitos [eram] sábios segundo a carne, não muitos poderosos, não muitos de nobre nascimento.
pt.B: Olhem para o chamado de vocês mesmos, {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}. Quando Deus os chamou, não muitos de vocês eram sábios pelos padrões humanos, não muitos tinham poder, não muitos vinham de famílias importantes.
pt.R: {{gender:Irmãos e irmãs|Irmãos}}, pensem em quem vocês eram quando Deus os chamou. Não muitos de vocês eram sábios aos olhos das outras pessoas. Não muitos eram importantes ou poderosos. Não muitos vinham de famílias importantes.

decisions.choice: look at: an appeal to consider what they can see for themselves
decisions.reason: Βλέπετε can be a command ("look at") or a statement ("you see"). Either way Paul points to the church itself as proof of what he has said.

decisions.choice: your calling: God's call that brought you to faith, and the kind of people you were when it came
alternatives: your job or position in life
decisions.reason: κλῆσιν is God's act of calling (verses 2, 9, 24). Here Paul asks them to think of who they were when the call came. In 7:20 the word comes close to meaning one's position in life.

decisions.choice: according to the flesh: by human standards
decisions.reason: κατὰ σάρκα means judged as people judge, apart from God, as in Philippians 3:3-4. The phrase may belong to all three lines.

decisions.choice: powerful and well-born: people of influence and of noble family
decisions.reason: Corinth was a Roman colony where rank, wealth and family mattered greatly. δυνατοί are people of power and influence; εὐγενεῖς are people of good birth. "Not many" means that a few were: Crispus, Gaius, and Erastus the city treasurer (Romans 16:23).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

decisions.choice: as people measure wisdom (B); in the eyes of other people (R)
decisions.reason: In everyday English "flesh" means the body; Balanced and Readable give the sense (m3).

decisions.choice: When God called you (B); who you were when God called you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "your calling" refers to here (m2).

decisions.choice: selon la chair (L); selon les critères humains (B); aux yeux des autres (R) (for the whole book: la chair at Literal, the sense at Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "la chair" at Balanced, but the Corinthians term sheet and the English Balanced give the sense "by human standards" here (m3), and French "selon la chair" would be heard as "in the body". Literal keeps the word.

decisions.choice: kwa kadiri ya mwili (L); kwa vipimo vya kibinadamu (B)
decisions.reason: For "flesh" in the sense of human standards, Literal keeps "mwili" as Swahili Romans 1:3 does, and Balanced says what it means, "by human measures". "Kimwili" would suggest the body.

decisions.choice: "theo xác thịt" (L); "theo cách người đời đánh giá" (B); "trong mắt người khác" (R) for "according to the flesh"
decisions.reason: "Xác thịt" is kept for sarx at Literal through the letter, as in the Vietnamese Colossians; here it means human standards (m3), so Balanced and Readable say that, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "vì hãy xem" (L), with the address first
decisions.reason: The Greek verb may be a command or a statement; Literal reads it as a command, as the English does, and keeps the little word "for".

decisions.choice: "육신을 따라" (L); "사람의 기준으로" (B); "다른 사람들이 보기에" (R), for "according to the flesh" through the letter
decisions.reason: "육신" is the word of Romans and Galatians for the flesh; Balanced and Readable give the sense the meaning decision describes, human standards, as the English does.

decisions.choice: segundo a carne (L); pelos padrões humanos (B); aos olhos das outras pessoas (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as docs/corinthians-terms.md sets the word: Literal says "a carne"; Balanced gives the sense, "pelos padrões humanos", "meramente humano", where the style guide would otherwise keep "carne", because in these letters the word mostly means human standards (m3) and the book-wide choice holds in Portuguese.

source.text: ἀλλὰ τὰ μωρὰ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελέξατο ὁ θεός, ἵνα καταισχύνῃ τοὺς σοφούς, καὶ τὰ ἀσθενῆ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελέξατο ὁ θεός, ἵνα καταισχύνῃ τὰ ἰσχυρά, καὶ τὰ ἀγενῆ τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τὰ ἐξουθενημένα ἐξελέξατο ὁ θεός, τὰ μὴ ὄντα, ἵνα τὰ ὄντα καταργήσῃ, ὅπως μὴ καυχήσηται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: But the foolish [things] of the world chose the God, so that he might shame the wise, and the weak [things] of the world chose the God, so that he might shame the strong [things], \v 28 and the low-born [things] of the world and the despised [things] chose the God, the [things] not being, so that the [things] being he might bring to nothing, \v 29 so that not may boast all flesh before the God.

en.L: But God chose the foolish things of the world so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might put the wise to shame, and God chose the weak things of the world so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might put the strong things to shame, \v 28 and God chose the low-born things of the world and the despised things, the things that are not, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might bring to nothing the things that are, \v 29 so that no flesh might boast before God.
en.B: Instead, God chose what the world counts foolish, to put the wise to shame. God chose what the world counts weak, to put the strong to shame. \v 28 God chose what the world counts low and despises, things that are nothing, to cancel out the things that are something, \v 29 so that no human being could ever boast in God's presence.
en.R: But God chose people the world thinks are foolish, to make wise people ashamed. God chose people the world thinks are weak, to make the strong ashamed. \v 28 God chose people the world looks down on and thinks are not important, people who seem to be nothing. He did this to bring to nothing the people who seem to be something. \v 29 So no one can ever boast in front of God.

fr.L: Mais Dieu a choisi les choses folles du monde afin de couvrir de honte les sages, et Dieu a choisi les choses faibles du monde afin de couvrir de honte les choses fortes, \v 28 et Dieu a choisi les choses du monde de basse naissance et les choses méprisées, les choses qui ne sont pas, afin de réduire à néant les choses qui sont, \v 29 afin que nulle chair ne se vante devant Dieu.
fr.B: Au contraire, Dieu a choisi ce que le monde tient pour fou, pour couvrir de honte les sages. Dieu a choisi ce que le monde tient pour faible, pour couvrir de honte ce qui est fort. \v 28 Dieu a choisi ce que le monde tient pour vil et ce qu’il méprise, ce qui n’est rien, pour annuler ce qui est quelque chose, \v 29 afin qu’aucun être humain ne puisse jamais se vanter devant Dieu.
fr.R: Mais Dieu a choisi des gens que le monde trouve fous, pour faire honte aux sages. Dieu a choisi des gens que le monde trouve faibles, pour faire honte aux forts. \v 28 Dieu a choisi des gens que le monde regarde de haut et trouve sans importance, des gens qui semblent n’être rien. Il l’a fait pour réduire à rien ceux qui semblent être quelque chose. \v 29 Ainsi, personne ne peut jamais se vanter devant Dieu.

sw.L: Lakini Mungu alivichagua vitu vya kipumbavu vya ulimwengu ili awaaibishe wenye hekima, na Mungu alivichagua vitu dhaifu vya ulimwengu ili avitie aibu vitu vyenye nguvu, \v 28 na Mungu alivichagua vitu duni vya ulimwengu na vitu vinavyodharauliwa, vitu visivyokuwako, ili avibatilishe vitu vilivyoko, \v 29 ili mwili wowote usijivune mbele za Mungu.
sw.B: Badala yake, Mungu alichagua kile ambacho ulimwengu unakiona kuwa upumbavu, ili awaaibishe wenye hekima. Mungu alichagua kile ambacho ulimwengu unakiona kuwa dhaifu, ili awaaibishe wenye nguvu. \v 28 Mungu alichagua kile ambacho ulimwengu unakiona kuwa duni na kukidharau, mambo yasiyo kitu, ili ayabatilishe mambo yaliyo kitu, \v 29 ili mwanadamu yeyote asipate kamwe kujivuna mbele za Mungu.
sw.R: Lakini Mungu aliwachagua watu ambao ulimwengu unawaona kuwa wapumbavu, ili awaaibishe watu wenye hekima. Mungu aliwachagua watu ambao ulimwengu unawaona kuwa dhaifu, ili awaaibishe wenye nguvu. \v 28 Mungu aliwachagua watu ambao ulimwengu unawadharau na kuwaona kuwa si muhimu, watu wanaoonekana kuwa si kitu. Alifanya hivyo ili awafanye kuwa si kitu wale wanaoonekana kuwa kitu. \v 29 Kwa hiyo hakuna mtu atakayeweza kamwe kujivuna mbele za Mungu.

es.L: Pero lo necio del mundo escogió Dios para avergonzar a los sabios, y lo débil del mundo escogió Dios para avergonzar a lo fuerte, \v 28 y lo bajo del mundo y lo despreciado escogió Dios, lo que no es, para anular lo que es, \v 29 para que ninguna carne se gloríe delante de Dios.
es.B: Al contrario, Dios escogió lo que el mundo tiene por necio, para avergonzar a los sabios. Dios escogió lo que el mundo tiene por débil, para avergonzar a los fuertes. \v 28 Dios escogió lo que el mundo tiene por bajo y desprecia, lo que no es nada, para anular lo que es algo, \v 29 a fin de que ningún ser humano pueda jamás gloriarse delante de Dios.
es.R: Pero Dios escogió a gente que el mundo considera tonta, para avergonzar a los sabios. Dios escogió a gente que el mundo considera débil, para avergonzar a los fuertes. \v 28 Dios escogió a gente que el mundo desprecia y considera sin importancia, gente que parece no ser nada. Lo hizo para reducir a nada a los que parecen ser algo. \v 29 Así nadie podrá jamás gloriarse delante de Dios.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn những điều dại dột của thế gian để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm hổ thẹn những người khôn ngoan, và Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn những điều yếu đuối của thế gian để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm hổ thẹn những điều mạnh mẽ, \v 28 và Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn những điều thấp hèn của thế gian và những điều bị khinh miệt, là những điều không có, để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm cho những điều đang có trở nên vô hiệu, \v 29 để không xác thịt nào có thể khoe mình trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Trái lại, Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn những gì thế gian cho là dại dột để làm hổ thẹn những người khôn ngoan. Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn những gì thế gian cho là yếu đuối để làm hổ thẹn những kẻ mạnh. \v 28 Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn những gì thế gian coi là thấp hèn và khinh miệt, những gì chẳng ra gì, để xóa bỏ những gì được coi là quan trọng, \v 29 để không một con người nào có thể khoe mình trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn những người mà thế gian cho là dại dột, để làm cho những người khôn ngoan phải xấu hổ. Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn những người mà thế gian cho là yếu đuối, để làm cho những người mạnh mẽ phải xấu hổ. \v 28 Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn những người mà thế gian coi thường và cho là không quan trọng, những người dường như chẳng là gì cả. Ngài làm như vậy để làm cho những người tưởng mình là quan trọng trở thành chẳng là gì. \v 29 Vì vậy, không ai có thể khoe mình trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그러나 하나님께서는 지혜로운 사람들을 부끄럽게 하시려고 세상의 어리석은 것들을 택하셨고, 강한 것들을 부끄럽게 하시려고 세상의 약한 것들을 택하셨습니다. \v 28 또 하나님께서는 있는 것들을 없애시려고 세상의 천한 것들과 멸시받는 것들, 곧 없는 것들을 택하셨습니다. \v 29 이는 어떤 육체도 하나님 앞에서 자랑하지 못하게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 오히려 하나님께서는 세상이 어리석다고 여기는 것들을 택하셔서 지혜로운 사람들을 부끄럽게 하셨습니다. 세상이 약하다고 여기는 것들을 택하셔서 강한 사람들을 부끄럽게 하셨습니다. \v 28 세상이 천하게 여기고 업신여기는 것들, 아무것도 아닌 것들을 택하셔서, 대단하다고 하는 것들을 무력하게 만드셨습니다. \v 29 그래서 어떤 사람도 하나님 앞에서 자랑할 수 없게 하셨습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 하나님께서는 세상이 어리석다고 생각하는 사람들을 택하셔서 지혜로운 사람들을 부끄럽게 하셨습니다. 세상이 약하다고 생각하는 사람들을 택하셔서 강한 사람들을 부끄럽게 하셨습니다. \v 28 하나님께서는 세상이 깔보고 중요하지 않다고 생각하는 사람들, 아무것도 아닌 것처럼 보이는 사람들을 택하셨습니다. 그렇게 하셔서 대단해 보이는 사람들을 아무것도 아니게 만드셨습니다. \v 29 그러니 아무도 하나님 앞에서 자랑할 수 없습니다.

pt.L: Mas Deus escolheu as [coisas] loucas do mundo para envergonhar os sábios, e Deus escolheu as [coisas] fracas do mundo para envergonhar as [coisas] fortes, \v 28 e Deus escolheu as [coisas] sem nobreza do mundo e as desprezadas, as que não são, para reduzir a nada as que são, \v 29 para que nenhuma carne se glorie diante de Deus.
pt.B: Pelo contrário, Deus escolheu o que o mundo considera louco para envergonhar os sábios. Deus escolheu o que o mundo considera fraco para envergonhar os fortes. \v 28 Deus escolheu o que o mundo considera baixo e despreza, coisas que nada são, para anular as que são alguma coisa, \v 29 a fim de que nenhum ser humano jamais possa se orgulhar na presença de Deus.
pt.R: Mas Deus escolheu pessoas que o mundo acha tolas, para envergonhar os sábios. Deus escolheu pessoas que o mundo acha fracas, para envergonhar os fortes. \v 28 Deus escolheu pessoas que o mundo despreza e acha que não têm importância, pessoas que parecem não ser nada. Ele fez isso para reduzir a nada as pessoas que parecem ser alguma coisa. \v 29 Assim ninguém pode jamais se orgulhar de nada diante de Deus.

decisions.choice: the foolish things, the weak things: people, spoken of as things, the Corinthians themselves among them
decisions.reason: The forms are neuter plural (μωρὰ, ἀσθενῆ), but after verse 26 Paul means people: those the world thinks little of. The neuter makes the description general and blunt. Against them stand "the wise" (σοφούς, masculine) and "the strong things".

decisions.choice: of the world: foolish, weak and low in the world's eyes
alternatives: the foolish people who are part of the world
decisions.reason: The genitive τοῦ κόσμου can mean "belonging to the world" or "as the world sees it". The contrast with God's choice favors the second: they are foolish by the world's measure, not by God's.

decisions.choice: the things that are not: people who count for nothing; to bring to nothing: to cancel the power of those who count for something
alternatives: things that do not exist at all
decisions.reason: μὴ ὄντα ("not being") means those who are nobodies in the world's eyes. καταργήσῃ means to make powerless or put out of action (2:6; 15:24). The words may recall God who calls into being things that are not (Romans 4:17): God's choice makes something of nobodies.

decisions.choice: all flesh: every human being
decisions.reason: πᾶσα σὰρξ is an Old Testament way of saying "every person", stressing human weakness before God (Isaiah 40:5-6). No one can claim credit before God; Jeremiah's words in verse 31 say the same.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the things that are not" without "and"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "and" before "the things that are not", making it one more item in the list. The SBLGNT follows important early manuscripts without it, so the phrase sums up the list: the low and despised are "things that are not". Reviewers should check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: what the world counts foolish ... weak ... low
alternatives: the foolish things of the world
decisions.reason: Balanced states the sense chosen in m2.

decisions.choice: people the world thinks are foolish ... weak ... looks down on
alternatives: the foolish things of the world
decisions.reason: Readable says that Paul is speaking of people (m1).

decisions.choice: no human being (B); no one (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom means every person (m4); Literal keeps "flesh".

decisions.choice: He did this to bring to nothing ...
alternatives: to bring to nothing the things that are
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long sentence and makes God the subject of a new one.

decisions.choice: se vanter at Literal throughout; at Balanced and Readable where the argument turns on the word (here and 1:31), "être fier", "tirer fierté" elsewhere (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the Corinthians term sheet settles for English "boast": Literal keeps one word family so it can be traced. "Se glorifier" is the traditional French, but it would blur with "glorifier", kept for giving glory. Each departure at Balanced and Readable has its own decision.

decisions.choice: gloriarse (L, B, R here and in verse 31)
decisions.reason: Literal says "gloriarse" for this word family throughout the letter (the noun too, 5:6), never "gloria", which is kept for another Greek word, so it can be traced, as Galatians 6 and Romans 5 do. Where Paul's argument turns on the word itself, as in 1:29-31, Balanced and Readable keep it too; elsewhere they say "sentirse orgulloso" or, for pride that takes credit for a gift, "presumir", each with a decision. "Jactarse" sounds only like bragging and would not fit 1:31.

decisions.choice: lo necio del mundo escogió Dios
alternatives: Dios escogió lo necio del mundo
decisions.reason: Spanish can put the object first, as the Greek does, so Literal keeps "the foolish things of the world" at the head of each clause, where the weight falls.

decisions.choice: kujivuna / kujivunia
decisions.reason: Book-wide choice for Paul's boasting words: Literal always uses "kujivuna" (to boast, with no object) and "kujivunia" (to boast in or about something), so the word can be traced. Balanced and Readable keep them here and in verse 31, where the argument turns on the word itself, and elsewhere say "kuona fahari" (take pride), "kujisifu" or "kujigamba" (brag) as the English guide's levels do, with a decision each time.

decisions.choice: "khoe mình" at every level in 1:29-31
decisions.reason: The founder settled that "boast" is kept wherever Paul's argument turns on the word itself, as in 1:29-31; "khoe mình" is the Literal word of the Vietnamese Romans and Galatians. Elsewhere in the letter Balanced and Readable say "tự hào" where the pride is not blamed, as in those letters.

decisions.choice: "không xác thịt nào" (L) for "no flesh"
decisions.reason: As in Romans 3:20, Literal keeps the Greek picture; Balanced says "no human being" and Readable "no one", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "자랑하다" at every level here and in verses 30-31
decisions.reason: The founder's choice for boasting keeps "boast" where Paul's argument turns on the word itself, as here. Korean "자랑" covers both bad and good pride, as Romans and Philippians use it; through the letter Literal keeps "자랑하다" always, and Balanced and Readable change it only where the English moves to "be proud" or "brag".

decisions.choice: "어떤 육체도" (L); "어떤 사람도" (B); "아무도" (R)
decisions.reason: As Romans 3:20 and Galatians 2:16: Literal keeps "flesh", and the other levels say "no human being".

decisions.choice: se glorie (L); se orgulhar (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book and Paul's letters, as the coordinating editor set it for Portuguese: this word family is "gloriar-se", "motivo de glória" at Literal, so it can be traced, and "orgulhar-se", "motivo de orgulho" at Balanced and Readable, even where the English Balanced keeps "boast" (1:29-31); Readable says "gabar-se" only where the English Readable says "brag" or "show off". "Orgulhar-se" can be good or bad pride, as Paul's word can; "vangloriar-se" would always condemn, and "gloriar-se" is church language at the plainer levels.

source.text: ἐξ αὐτοῦ δὲ ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ὃς ἐγενήθη σοφία ἡμῖν ἀπὸ θεοῦ, δικαιοσύνη τε καὶ ἁγιασμὸς καὶ ἀπολύτρωσις, ἵνα καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὁ καυχώμενος ἐν κυρίῳ καυχάσθω.

records.literal_gloss: From him but you are in Christ Jesus, who became wisdom for us from God, righteousness both and holiness and redemption, \v 31 so that just as it has been written, The [one] boasting in [the] Lord let him boast.

en.L: But from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you are in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, who became wisdom for us from God, both righteousness and holiness and redemption, \v 31 so that, just as it is written, "The one who boasts must boast in [the] Lord."
en.B: It is God who has placed you in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has become God's wisdom for us, which means our righteousness, our holiness and our redemption. \v 31 So, as Scripture says, "Whoever boasts should boast in the Lord."
en.R: God is the one who has joined you to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} is God's wisdom for us. Because of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we are righteous in God's sight, we are made holy, and we are set free. \v 31 So, as Scripture says, "Anyone who wants to boast should boast only about the Lord."

fr.L: Or c’est de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que vous êtes {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, qui est devenu pour nous sagesse de la part de Dieu, et justice, et sainteté, et rédemption, \v 31 afin que, comme il est écrit : « Celui qui se vante, qu’il se vante dans le Seigneur. »
fr.B: C’est Dieu qui vous a placés {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est devenu pour nous la sagesse qui vient de Dieu, c’est-à-dire notre justice, notre sainteté et notre rédemption. \v 31 Ainsi, comme le dit l’Écriture : « Que celui qui se vante se vante dans le Seigneur. »
fr.R: C’est Dieu qui vous a unis au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est la sagesse de Dieu pour nous. Grâce à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, nous sommes justes aux yeux de Dieu, nous sommes rendus saints, et nous sommes libérés. \v 31 Ainsi, comme le dit l’Écriture : « Que celui qui veut se vanter ne se vante que du Seigneur. »

sw.L: Lakini kutokana na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ninyi mko katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, ambaye amekuwa hekima kwetu kutoka kwa Mungu, haki na utakaso na ukombozi pia, \v 31 ili, kama ilivyoandikwa, "Anayejivuna, ajivunie Bwana."
sw.B: Ni Mungu aliyewaweka ninyi katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} amekuwa hekima ya Mungu kwetu, yaani haki yetu, utakaso wetu na ukombozi wetu. \v 31 Kwa hiyo, kama Maandiko yasemavyo, "Yeyote anayejivuna, na ajivunie Bwana."
sw.R: Mungu ndiye aliyewaunganisha ninyi na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ndiye hekima ya Mungu kwa ajili yetu. Kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} tunahesabiwa haki mbele za Mungu, tunafanywa watakatifu, na tunawekwa huru. \v 31 Kwa hiyo, kama Maandiko yasemavyo, "Yeyote anayetaka kujivuna, amjivunie Bwana peke yake."

es.L: Pero de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:ustedes están|vosotros estáis}} en {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús, quien llegó a ser para nosotros sabiduría de parte de Dios, tanto justicia como santificación y redención, \v 31 para que, así como está escrito: «El que se gloría, que se gloríe en [el] Señor».
es.B: Es Dios quien {{plural_you:los|os}} ha puesto en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha llegado a ser para nosotros la sabiduría de Dios, es decir, nuestra justicia, nuestra santidad y nuestra redención. \v 31 Así, como dice la Escritura: «Quien quiera gloriarse, que se gloríe en el Señor».
es.R: Dios es quien {{plural_you:los|os}} ha unido {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}. {{christos:Cristo|El Mesías}} es la sabiduría de Dios para nosotros. Gracias a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, somos justos ante Dios, somos hechos santos y somos liberados. \v 31 Por eso, como dice la Escritura: «Si alguien quiere gloriarse, que se gloríe solo en el Señor».

vi.L: Nhưng bởi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà anh chị em ở trong {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} Giê-xu, là Đấng đã trở nên sự khôn ngoan cho chúng ta từ Đức Chúa Trời, cũng là sự công chính, sự nên thánh và sự cứu chuộc, \v 31 để, như có chép: "Người khoe mình hãy khoe mình trong Chúa."
vi.B: Chính Đức Chúa Trời đã đặt anh chị em ở trong Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã trở nên sự khôn ngoan của Đức Chúa Trời cho chúng ta, tức là sự công chính, sự nên thánh và sự cứu chuộc của chúng ta. \v 31 Vậy, như Kinh Thánh có chép: "Ai khoe mình, hãy khoe mình trong Chúa."
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời là Đấng đã kết hiệp anh chị em với Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} là sự khôn ngoan của Đức Chúa Trời cho chúng ta. Nhờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, chúng ta được công chính trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời, được nên thánh và được giải thoát. \v 31 Vậy, như Kinh Thánh chép: "Ai muốn khoe mình thì chỉ nên khoe mình về Chúa."

ko.L: 여러분이 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에 있는 것은 그분에게서 [난 것]입니다. {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 우리에게 하나님에게서 온 지혜가 되셨으니, 곧 의와 거룩함과 구속이 [되셨습니다]. \v 31 그것은 기록된 바와 같이 "자랑하는 사람은 주 안에서 자랑하라" 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 여러분을 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 안에 있게 하신 분은 하나님이십니다. {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 우리에게 하나님에게서 온 지혜가 되셨습니다. 그 지혜는 곧 우리의 의와 거룩함과 구속입니다. \v 31 그러므로 성경에 기록된 대로 "자랑하려는 사람은 주님을 자랑하라" 하는 말씀이 이루어집니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 여러분을 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수와 하나가 되게 하셨습니다. {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 하나님께서 우리에게 주신 지혜이십니다. 그분 덕분에 우리는 하나님 앞에서 의로운 사람이 되고, 거룩하게 되고, 자유롭게 되었습니다. \v 31 그러므로 성경에 이렇게 쓰여 있습니다. "자랑하고 싶은 사람은 오직 주님만 자랑하라."

pt.L: Mas da parte {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} vocês estão {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus, que se tornou para nós sabedoria da parte de Deus, tanto justiça como santificação e redenção, \v 31 para que, como está escrito: "Quem se gloria, deve se gloriar no Senhor."
pt.B: É Deus quem colocou vocês {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} se tornou para nós a sabedoria de Deus, isto é, a nossa justiça, a nossa santificação e a nossa redenção. \v 31 Assim, como dizem as Escrituras: "Quem quiser se orgulhar, que se orgulhe do Senhor."
pt.R: Foi Deus quem uniu vocês {{christos:a Cristo|ao Messias}} Jesus. {{christos:Cristo|O Messias}} é a sabedoria de Deus para nós. Por causa {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, somos justos diante de Deus, somos feitos santos e somos libertados. \v 31 Assim, como dizem as Escrituras: "Quem quiser se orgulhar, que se orgulhe somente do Senhor."

decisions.choice: from him: God is the source; their being in Christ is his doing
decisions.reason: αὐτοῦ refers back to God, named at the end of verse 29. Their new life "in Christ Jesus" comes from God, not from their own wisdom or rank, so there is nothing to boast of.

decisions.choice: righteousness, holiness and redemption spell out what "wisdom from God" is
alternatives: four separate gifts: wisdom, righteousness, holiness and redemption
decisions.reason: τε καὶ ("both ... and") ties the last three words closely together and sets them a little apart from σοφία. The point of the passage is wisdom, so the three most likely explain what God's wisdom in Christ is: not clever ideas, but what Christ has done for us. Read as four gifts, the sense is close.

decisions.choice: righteousness: being in the right with God, given in Christ
decisions.reason: δικαιοσύνη here is what Christ is "for us": the right standing with God that God gives (2 Corinthians 5:21; Philippians 3:9).

decisions.choice: holiness: being set apart for God, made his own
alternatives: a gradual process of moral improvement only
decisions.reason: ἁγιασμὸς belongs with "made holy" and "holy ones" in verse 2: in Christ they belong to God.

decisions.choice: redemption: release, as of a slave set free
alternatives: the payment of a price, as the main idea
decisions.reason: ἀπολύτρωσις means setting free, as a slave or captive was set free (Colossians 1:14). Paul will remind the Corinthians that they were bought with a price (6:20; 7:23).

decisions.choice: a shortened quotation of Jeremiah 9:23-24 (9:22-23 in the Hebrew numbering)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 9:23-24 says: let not the wise boast of wisdom, nor the mighty of might, nor the rich of riches, but let the one who boasts boast of this, that he understands and knows God. These are the very people of verse 26: the wise, the powerful and the well-born. Paul sums up the passage in one line; the Greek of 1 Samuel 2:10 has similar words. He uses the same line in 2 Corinthians 10:17.

decisions.choice: the Lord: in Jeremiah, God's own name; here most likely Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Jeremiah 9:24 the word is the divine name, YHWH. Paul quotes it with κυρίῳ ("Lord"), and after verse 30, where everything comes to believers "in Christ Jesus", the Lord in whom they boast is most likely Christ. As with "calling on the name of the Lord" (verse 2), a text about God himself is applied to Jesus.

decisions.choice: so that: Paul leaves the verb unspoken, "so that it may be as it is written"
decisions.reason: ἵνα is followed directly by the quotation, with no verb of its own. The sense is clear: God has acted in this way so that the Scripture may hold true.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. Readable supplies the title again where it begins a new sentence.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "the LORD" for the divine name in the Old Testament itself. Here Paul quotes the verse with the Greek word for "Lord", as John 1:23 does; meaning decision m7 explains whom it means.

decisions.choice: It is God who has placed you in (B); God is the one who has joined you to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the source (m1).

decisions.choice: we are righteous in God's sight
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key term as "righteous" and says what it means here (m3).

decisions.choice: The one who boasts must boast (L); Whoever boasts should boast (B); Anyone who wants to boast should boast only (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is a command in the third person. English has no exact match, so each level uses "must" or "should" and avoids a masculine pronoun for a saying that applies to anyone.

decisions.choice: la justice (L, B); justes aux yeux de Dieu (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the style guide: "la justice" is the key term at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what it means here, being in the right with God (m3), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: « Celui qui se vante, qu'il se vante » (L); « Que celui qui se vante se vante » (B); « Que celui qui veut se vanter ne se vante que » (R)
alternatives: « Celui qui se vante doit se vanter »
decisions.reason: French has a third-person command with "que", so it renders the Greek form directly; "celui qui" is already generic. Literal keeps the Greek order with a resumptive "qu'il".

decisions.choice: santificación (L); santidad (B)
decisions.reason: As in Romans 6:19: Literal keeps "santificación", the word built like the Greek noun; Balanced says "santidad", as the English Balanced says "holiness", since the sense is being set apart for God (m4).

decisions.choice: utakaso
decisions.reason: "Utakaso" is being made holy, set apart for God, which is the sense the meaning decision gives and the word Swahili Romans 6:19, 22 uses; it shares its root with "waliotakaswa" in 1:2. Readable says "tunafanywa watakatifu".

decisions.choice: tunahesabiwa haki mbele za Mungu
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key term "haki" in the phrase settled in Swahili Romans for being put right with God.

decisions.choice: "Chúa" in the quotation, not "CHÚA"
decisions.reason: The Greek has kyrios, and Paul most likely means Christ (m7); the capitals of the divine name are kept for the Hebrew of the Old Testament itself, as the Vietnamese Romans does in its quotations (10:13).

decisions.choice: "sự công chính, sự nên thánh và sự cứu chuộc" (L, B); "được công chính trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời, được nên thánh và được giải thoát" (R)
decisions.reason: The key terms of the Vietnamese Romans: "sự công chính" (1:17), "sự nên thánh" (6:19), "sự cứu chuộc" (3:24). Readable turns them into what happens to us, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "의", "거룩함", "구속" (L, B); "하나님 앞에서 의로운 사람", "거룩하게 되다", "자유롭게 되다" (R)
decisions.reason: "의" is a key term, the same word at every level, which Readable keeps in "의로운 사람"; "구속" is the word of Romans 3:24 and Colossians 1:14 for redemption, and Readable says what it means, as Romans 3:24 does.

decisions.choice: "주" (L); "주님" (B, R), with no divine_name span
decisions.reason: In Jeremiah the word is the divine name; Paul's Greek has "Lord", and the meaning decision reads it here as Christ, so Korean says "주" in Literal, as Romans does in quotations, and "주님" at the other levels.

decisions.choice: Quem quiser se orgulhar, que se orgulhe (B, R); Quem se gloria, deve se gloriar (L)
alternatives: Aquele que se gloria, glorie-se no Senhor
decisions.reason: Portuguese has a third-person command, the subjunctive "que se orgulhe", so Balanced and Readable need no "must" or "should", and "quem" already covers anyone. Literal says "deve", as the English Literal says "must".
